News.title: Romance fraudster posed as Army veteran who flew with Prince Harry to fleece two women out of £14k in ‘calculated’ con
News.content:
CON THE PULL Romance fraudster posed as Army veteran who flew with Prince Harry to fleece two women out of £14k in ‘calculated’ con

A ROMANCE fraudster posed as an Army veteran who flew with Prince Harry to swindle two women out of more than £14,500.

David Griffiths, 52, targeted two professional women in a “cold and calculated” scam to steal money from them after meeting on dating apps.



A court heard Griffiths told a web of lies to impress the victims including that he had served in the Air Army Corps and had a job as a search and rescue pilot.

But the alarm was raised after he swindled thousands of pounds from them between July 2022 and May 2024.



He asked the women to invest in businesses, holidays or properties with him before fleecing them of thousands.

Cardiff Crown Court heard the victims felt they “won’t be able to trust again” after they were conned by the romance fraudster.

Prosecutor David Pinnell said Griffiths lied “about his occupation, his wealth, his military past and his future and past purchase of properties”.

The frauds were carried out on one woman in Pontypool, South Wales, and another near Bristol – costing them £4,500 and £10,178.14.



Victim Helen Moorefield said: “He groomed me to have sex to get financial gain for himself.”

“I believe this man has done this to other women, I do not believe we’re the only ones.”

Businesswoman Helen, 57, said: “He showed me pictures of his Army life.

“He explained to me he flew in the Army with Prince Harry… that he’d been shot down in one of his helicopters.”

But Helen later began to become suspicious at Griffiths’ excuses for never having money despite his claimed wealth and used Clare’s Law to uncover he had previous conviction for fraud.



Fellow victim Joanne Brandon-Hodgkinson said Griffiths told her of his fictional Army career and claimed he earned £120,000-a-year as an operations director for a helicopter company in London’s Canary Wharf.

But months into their relationship he claimed he had a new job at RAF St Athan and could not meet her due to shift patterns.

“I am now convinced that during that period he was probably living a separate life with somebody else.” she said.

Griffiths, of Castlemorton, Malvern, pleaded guilty to two counts of fraud.

Judge Paul Hobson told him you “simply didn’t care” about your victims as you told “whopping lies”.



Griffiths will face a proceeds of crime hearing on November 23.

News.title: Watch as bungling airport workers crash baggage conveyor belt into passenger plane’s engine leaving driver injured
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment bungling airport workers crash a baggage conveyor belt into a plane’s engine, leaving the driver injured.

Dramatic footage shows the aftermath of the crash with one side of the aircraft caved in due to the force of the collision.



A section of the plane can be seen hanging off as torch light reveals the full extent of the damage.

The incident took place only moments after passengers safely disembarked Air Peace flight P47427.



The Airbus A320, which departed from Kano, Nigeria landed safely at Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos on Tuesday night.

The staff member operating the vehicle reportedly slumped to the ground after ramming into the aircraft.



Paramedics rushed to the scene, administering first aid to the victim.

The damaged plane was due to operate several more flights in the coming days, but has now been decommissioned for repairs.



Air Peace confirmed the collision caused significant damage, disrupting the schedule.

A spokesperson said: “We sincerely apologise to our esteemed passengers whose travel plans may be affected by this unforeseen ground handling incident.”

They added that customer service teams were providing alternative options and assistance where possible.

An investigation is now ongoing to determine the exact circumstances of the incident.

Operations are expected to return to normal once a replacement aircraft is found.



This comes after a baggage handler was left in critical condition when her scarf got caught in a conveyor belt at Heathrow.

The woman was violently dragged along by the machinery after all passengers had disembarked the plane.

Colleagues inside Loganair Flight 82WR from Dundee and on the other side of the plane were reportedly oblivious to what was happening.

“It was the stuff of nightmares,” a source said.

“No one was on hand to help out. It’s a miracle she wasn’t killed.”



The experienced team leader for Menzies was later treated by paramedics and taken to hospital.

A London Ambulance Service spokesperson said: “We were called at 5.49pm on Wednesday 14 February to reports of an incident on Terminal 2 Heathrow Airport, Hounslow.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We sent resources to the scene, including an ambulance crew, an advanced paramedic and members of our hazardous area response team.

“Our first medics arrived on scene in four minutes. We treated a patient at the scene and took them to a major trauma centre as a priority.”

News.title: Asylum seeker, 43, with STD raped vulnerable man, 20, in park after luring him to ‘secluded’ area
News.content:
HORRIFIC ATTACK Asylum seeker, 43, with STD raped vulnerable man, 20, in park after luring him to ‘secluded’ area

AN ASYLUM seeker with an STD who raped a vulnerable man in a park after luring him to a secluded area has been jailed.

Islamuddin Talash, 43, raped the 20-year-old, who had run away from home, in Abbey Park Leicester in October 2023.



Leicester Crown Court was told that Talash invited the younger man back to his hotel where he said he had a bike that he could give him.

It was heard that the 20-year-old had been approaching strangers in the hopes of buying a bike.



Talash proceeded to take the vulnerable man to a secluded area of the park before attacking him.

He was found guilty of one count of rape following a trial in June after he stood trial twice before.

Recorder Sacha Ackland sentenced the 43-year-old to six years in prison yesterday, minus the time he had spent on remand.

On the completion of his sentence, Talash, an Afghan national, will be liable to automatic deportation.

Leicester Crown Court heard that the 20-year-old had never visited Leicester before.

It was heard he had conditions that impacted his social functioning and reduced his ability to recognise danger.



Ackland said the victim was “in need of assistance” and he “naively decided to trust you [Talash].”

It was heard Talash lured the victim to an area of the park that was clearly used by people having sex – with condoms littering the ground.

Talash is then alleged to have demanded the victim perform oral sex on him, to which the 20-year-old “reluctantly agreed.”

Ackland told Talash the victim took the “path of least resistance”, not recognising “you would do further.”

Prosecutor Paul Cavin KC said an aggravating factor to the case was Talash leaving the victim open to contracting an STI.



Talash had an STD at the time of the assault, which he was taking medication for.

Despite not contracting the disease, the victim had to undergo treatment.

Ackland said: “I’m sure at least on some level you knew you were exposing him to a risk of contracting the disease.”

Defending Talash, Tom Welshman said the offence was serious but added that he had a “number of points to make professionally”.

He went on to say a number of Talash’s family members had been killed in Afghanistan and that he had come to Britain to “escape a hellish existence.”



In mitigation, Welshman said Talash had no previous convictions.

Before meeting Talash the victim had encountered two teenagers who recognised he was vulnerable.

The pair kept an eye on him and when they realised what had happened, they took the 20- year-old to a police station to report the rape.

It was heard they had both come to court three times in the past two years to “ensure justice was done.”

Ackland said the two teenagers would receive £250 each.



Detective Sergeant Sarah Jones was the officer in the case. She said: “The actions of the witnesses on that day were crucial in this investigation, they did absolutely the right thing by acting on their suspicions.

“They, along with the victim, deserve enormous credit for giving an account in court that led to today’s outcome.

“The two boys were able to provide an image and footage which assisted officers in getting a positive identification.

“An officer who was working within our team took it on herself to do a walk-through the park and immediately spotted a man and recalled his similarities to the man in the image provided by the witnesses.

“He was arrested straight away and charged within hours. This outcome is a testament to the great work that went into the investigation and the strength of evidence secured this result.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The victim was vulnerable, and the defendant used this for his own sexual gratification.

“We hope that this case reassures the local community and helps the victim put the events of that afternoon behind him.”

News.title: Mother of tragic woman who died by euthanasia after gang-rape ordeal hunts her attackers after details left in diary
News.content:
THE mum of the Spanish woman who died by euthanasia after a gang-rape has launched a hunt for her attackers.

Noelia Castillo, 25, died by euthanasia in March after a two-year battle with the courts.



Her mum Yolanda Ramos has begged Spanish cops to act after reading harrowing details of a gang rape written in her daughter’s diary.

Yolanda said: “I have decided to report the men who caused my daughter so much harm.



“I am doing this because I feel it is what she wanted.”

Christian Lawyers asked the prosecutor to find those responsible.



Noelia claimed she was raped by her ex-partner, who she had a four-year relationship with.

She said the second alleged rape took place in Salou, where she alleged she was drugged by a waiter.

Noelia then said three men raped her.

How to get help EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers. It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes. And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. If you, or anyone you know, needs help dealing with mental health problems, the following organisations provide support: CALM, www.thecalmzone.net, 0800 585 858

Heads Together,www.headstogether.org.uk

HUMEN www.wearehumen.org

Mind, www.mind.org.uk, 0300 123 3393

Papyrus, www.papyrus-uk.org, 0800 068 41 41

Samaritans,www.samaritans.org, 116 123



The gang rape drove the young women to attempt suicide, she said in interviews before her death.

Noelia was paraplegic and in constant pain after attempting to take her own life by jumping from a fifth-floor window.

She is one of the youngest people in Spain to die by euthanasia.

Her dad, Geronimo Castillo, waged a lengthy legal fight to try to get judges to block his daughter’s euthanasia request with the support of the conservative group Christian Lawyers.

But Noelia, who spoke openly about her decision to end the mental and physical pain she has suffered for years in a TV interview, said she wanted to “leave in peace”.



She said she had been raped by her partner when she had taken sleeping pills, assaulted by two men in a night club, and gang-raped by three men.

The gang-rape took place just three or four days before she attempted suicide in 2022, Noelia said.

She recounted both rapes to her mother before her death, lawyers confirmed, and had written details of them in her diary.

Mum Yolanda said: “Noelia spoke about the rapes on television, and on the very day she died, she gave me her diary.

“And when I read it, I understood many things.



“I feel that my daughter wanted the whole truth to come out someday.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“That’s why I’ve decided to go to the Prosecutor’s Office, because I can’t just stand idly by.”

News.title: Farmer died after becoming trapped under quad bike in freezing temperatures all night
News.content:
FARM TRAGEDY Farmer died after becoming trapped under quad bike in freezing temperatures all night

A FARMER died after becoming trapped under a quad bike for 16 hours in freezing temperatures, an inquest heard.

David Charles Knipe, 65, was found by his neighbour in the woods, trapped at the waist by the bike.



The poultry farmer also suffered from two cardiac arrests in Royal Preston Hospital the next morning, where he was airlifted to once found.

David, from Tebay, Cumbria, was found on December 6, 2024 underneath the quad, falling in and out of consciousness.



Assistant coroner at Workington Coroner’s Court, Craig Smith, concluded David had died of hypothermia as a result of the incident.

While the report into his death suspected a broken pelvis, this was not visible in the post-mortem examination.

It detailed: “It’s unlikely to have contributed to the death… With the absence of internal injuries, it’s highly likely he died of hypothermia.”

He was last seen in the evening on his land, High Carlingill farm, driving the vehicle into the woods.

David’s wife, Christine, told the coroner that if her husband had been on a newer model of the quad bike, it could have saved his life.

She said: “I believe now there’s technology available whereby a third party is alerted if a quad bike topples – I think that’s the part we found quite difficult.



“I’d think that sort of technology may help others going forward – we’re aware that farms are dangerous places.”

At the time of the tragic incident, Christine had left the farm with her daughter Bethany for a trip to Manchester.

While she was unable to make contact with her husband, the inquest heard that this was not out of the norm for David.

However, when her husband did not show up to the Milnthorpe’s market the next day, she began to worry.

When a neighbour was sent to check on David, he was found in Heart Wood, visible to the M6, trapped by the waist under his quad.



Mechanical engineer, Colin Dunn, informed the coroner that the quad bike had a number of faults including a missing brake lever on the handlebar.

David, who regularly serviced the vehicle, was assumed to have been riding across a steep slope over rough terrain when he became stuck.

It is thought that a combination of factors that affected the bike’s stability, resulting in his vehicle entrapping him.

These include the steepness of the slope, the difficulty of the trailer tow, the terrain, and the low tyre pressure.

In his conclusion, Mr Smith said: “[David] was a very competent and experienced driver, he was very familiar with [the quad’s] use in Heart Wood, there’s nothing in the evidence to suggest this wasn’t a momentary issue.”



David was a founding member of “award-winning farmers markets” in Cumbria, where he sold poultry and eggs.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He worked with supermarkets and councils to establish the markets in the country, and took pride in teaching the younger generation how to farm.

His wife, Christine, told the BBC: “He was liked and loved by many, not just the farming community.”

News.title: Chilling RIP text told me my son Harvey Willgoose, 15, was fatally stabbed at school… alarming red flags were missed
News.content:
DESPITE their best efforts, Caroline and Mark Willgoose had problems persuading their son, Harvey to attend school, because of his anxiety issues and increasing safety fears. So, when he happily announced one morning that he was going in, they were pleased.

His best friend, Ben, called for him and as he left, Harvey said to Caroline, “Shut the door behind me, Mum. I love you.”





Three hours later, the 15-year-old was dead, having been fatally stabbed by a fellow pupil who had been one of his best friends.

The Channel 4 documentary Murder Case: Digital Detectives looks into police analysis of CCTV footage at the school in Sheffield which captured the horrific incident and phone records that revealed a growing rift between the two friends as well as the killer, Umar Khan’s, obsession with weapons.

And in an exclusive interview with The Sun, Caroline opens up about the heartbreak of losing her son, how alarming danger signs from Umar were ignored and how she feels Harvey is constantly still with her, guiding her in her campaign to raise awareness of the danger of knives in schools.

“I hadn’t done any public speaking before and it’s weird but I don’t get nervous when talking at schools, youth clubs and even in front of the crowd at Sheffield United FC, who Harvey supported,” she says.

“I think I’m driven because it’s just so important to me to get the message out there for our Harvey. Maybe it’s a bit of therapy for me to talk about it but I feel 100 per cent that Harvey is guiding me through this.

“I just feel him sometimes. We’ve got a dog that we let sleep on our bed, and sometimes I feel a pressure, and I think, ‘Oh, the dog’s on the bed,’ but when I look, he’s not there.

“Harvey was always on my bed. When Mark went to work, Harvey would come and sit on my bed and chat or be on his phone. And I just know he’s still with me.”

Harvey was stabbed at around 12.15pm on 3 February 2025. As the school went into lockdown, Caroline was contacted by police and driven to the hospital where Harvey had been rushed to.





“When we got there, I looked at my phone and saw someone had said, ‘RIP Harvey,’” she recalls. “I showed it to the family liaison officer and she said, ‘Yes. He’s passed away.’ I just screamed. It was harrowing.”

Harvey had been declared dead before they could get him into hospital.

At the police station, Umar used his right to silence and made no reply to all questions.

But in a written statement, he said he had been racially abused previously and had taken a knife into school on that occasion, for the first time, to protect himself from others, including Harvey, who he thought was armed.

However, police found no evidence that Harvey had ever carried any weapons or was abusive.

In fact, as he told both his school and his parents, one of the reasons why he avoided school was because of other pupils taking weapons in. And it was Kumar who had the biggest reputation for doing that.

He would boast to other kids that he had a knife or an axe on him.

“I was in denial when Harvey said that,” admits Caroline. “I was like, ‘As if anybody’s going to take a knife into school.’ That’s what people think. I would never have thought that I would be talking about knife crime. I thought it was all gang related, but it’s not.”



DCI Joe Hackworthy, Deputy Senior Investigating Officer, recalls, “We looked into Umar’s background and found he had had a difficult upbringing.

“His mum suffered from mental health problems, his dad was not always around. There was poverty in the family, which was documented in social care records. There are accounts from Umar about having to look after his siblings.”

In fact, it was the second time that the school had gone into lockdown within a week – after Umar brought a knife in on the previous Wednesday. Two groups had fallen out, there had been a fight, with Umar aligned to one group and it seems like Harvey was on the other.

But Umar had been allowed to go back. On the very morning of the stabbing he had been asked by a teacher if he had brought in any kind of weapon. He had said he had not and was let in without a search of his bag.

Not surprisingly, Caroline is appalled by this. “If you’ve got a reason to ask, you’ve got a reason to search,” she says.

Just after lunchbreak, he pulled out a hunting knife he had bought online and plunged it into Harvey’s chest.

“We had been close mates, myself, Umar and Harvey,” says Ben. “The three of us would talk non-stop and make each other laugh. Our teacher called us the three amigos.

“I think Harvey saw that Umar wasn’t in the right mind set. Harvey kind of took him under his wing. No one really spoke to him as much as me and Harvey.”



“Harvey was everybody’s friend,” says Caroline.

“We only really argued about one thing and that was him not going to school.

“He suffered with anxiety and was a school avoider, which is a big thing now. There are one in five children who don’t go to school. A lot of it is from anxiety from being locked at home during COVID.

“We don’t know what that’s actually done to these kids. It stole a lot of their childhood being stuck at home and then, all of a sudden, opening the doors and saying, ‘Right, business as usual.’ And Harvey found going from a small primary to a massive school overwhelming.”

Umar’s obsession with weapons was apparent from a search of his phone by police, who found him looking for axes, zombie and Rambo knives to buy. There was also a video of him with a knife on school grounds.

Umar Khan was found guilty of murder and sentenced to life, with a minimum of 16 years.

St Clare Catholic Academy Trust commissioned an independent review in the aftermath of the stabbing. It identified several shortcomings in the school’s handling of safeguarding concerns.

As a result, the Department of Education issued the trust with a formal notice to improve.



Caroline was shocked when she read the report, the full version of which she wants released to the public so lessons can be learned.

“There were 133 incidences linking Umar with weapons, gangs and anger issues. He had taken a BB gun on a school trip but nothing was done about it.

“The same when he brought an axe into school. His mum informed the school he had it, but nothing was followed up properly. If they’d have looked at his phone, they’d have seen that he had an unhealthy interest in weapons. That was another missed opportunity.

“The problem is that a lot of schools are academies and they are run as businesses. One of my main aims is getting knife arches (metal detectors) into schools but the academies shy away from them because they think it shows that they’ve got a knife problem. It’s all about their reputation above the needs of children.

“When I go into schools and youth clubs, I also talk about Umar and his horrible life. The only time he showed any emotion was when he was in the dock at his trial and they mentioned his parents and his siblings and he started crying.

“Mark told me about this, because I was in another room. I couldn’t stand being in the main court room. And when he told me, I got upset. Mark asked me why I was crying and I said, ‘Because it’s so sad. From that one split decision, he ruined all these people’s lives.’ And he’s missing his family. When I talk to children about this, they seem to relate. They are like, ‘I never thought of it that way.’

“One of the things I am thinking of doing is going into schools with a balloon and getting them to write down two things that they couldn’t live without. One might be their mum and the other football, and then I pop the balloon and say, ‘That’s gone now.’ I think that might shock them.

“I feel like Harvey was put here for a reason, to change things. And that’s why I won’t stop until I’ve made things right for him.



“There are just so many signs of him all the time. Sometimes, when I’m talking, I think, ‘Has that actually come out of my mouth?’ It feels like I’m speaking for Harvey.

“I speak to him all the time. If I lose something I’ll say, ‘Find it for me, Harvey,’ and he does. I know it sounds daft but I feel like the dog feels him as well.

“At the bottom of the garden, his goal nets and his football are still there. We were doing a car boot sale once and Mark said, ‘I’ll take them,’ and I’m like, ‘Absolutely, no, you can’t. I can’t sell them. They’re Harvey’s.’

“I can’t throw anything away. His tops are still in the wash and in my ironing pile, and his school shoes are still there because he didn’t wear his school shoes that day. His kagool is still hung up and his bedroom is like it was. I keep the door shut though. I can’t stand it being open because I just I expect him to be there. The room still smells of him.

“Nobody will understand the pain. It’s exhausting. It’s just so sad when I see his friends. They look lost because he was always in the middle of it all. You know, he was the boss. A lot of his friends are on medication because of it. Having to lose him like that, is just unreal. Every morning I think, ‘Has it been a dream?’ And then you relive it.

“It’s horrible getting up in the morning. I don’t normally get up before 11 o’clock. I’m awake, and then look at my phone, because I get so many messages, and I have to tell myself it’s business as usual and answer emails and stuff.

“I lost my dad in in October because he got cancer just after Harvey’s funeral, and on his deathbed, he said, ‘Harvey is sat with me. I feel his pressure.’ I haven’t even cried for my dad because I know that they’re together.”

News.title: Britain’s Challenger 2 tanks being swapped for suicide drone fleet to protect Nato’s eastern flank from Putin
News.content:
BRITAIN is withdrawing its tanks from Estonia and replacing them with drones in a historic shift to how Nato defends its eastern frontier from Russia.

A fleet of new spy and attack drones will form a new kind of “anti-armour force” to devastate Russian invaders should Vladimir Putin launch an invasion.



The Ministry of Defence said the drone force would be faster, deadlier and harder to hit than the existing squadron of Challenger 2 tanks.

Some 400 extra troops will also surge into Estonia, bringing the total UK deployment to 1,200 personnel.



It comes amid US warnings that Moscow is planning a “major provocation” against the Baltic states or Poland now that Putin is on the back foot in Ukraine.

The MoD said the switch to drones, “reflects the realities of modern conflict”.

It is a major blow to the Challenger force after ten years on the frontline.

And it undermines Labour’s claim that tanks “remain essential” to defending Nato territory.

Labour’s Defence Investment Plan said tanks ensured land forces could “seize or defend ground in all environments and conditions”.

The MoD said the new drone force “will be able to deploy, disperse and demonstrate combat readiness more rapidly than a traditional armoured formation”.



The Mobile Anti-Armour Force includes spy drones and one way attack drones proven in Ukraine.

The MoD said its decision was made after “comprehensive war-gaming with Estonia”.

It claimed the new formation would, “deliver greater operational effect than the current armoured construct”.



It comes after Army Chief Roly Walker warned British drones in the Baltic State must be primed to strike Russia “within 30 minutes”.

Gen Walker told a conference last month: “If deterrence fails… the cost we impose on the aggressor must be felt immediately and preferably before they get out of their assembly areas.”

A squadron of British main battle tanks have been in Estonia since 2017, in response to Russia’s assaults on Ukraine and the capture of Crimea.



Estonia Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur said: “The decision to deploy additional troops reinforces the close cooperation between our two countries and the United Kingdom‘s long-term commitment to our shared security.”

“British troops train alongside the Estonian Defence Forces every day. In addition, a British Army brigade remains at high readiness in the United Kingdom to reinforce us if required.”

News.title: My sister was left brain dead after taking cocaine…how deadly superstrength batches are flooding UK streets
News.content:
A WOMAN whose sister was left brain dead after taking super-strength cocaine has sent an urgent warning to users as crime gangs flood UK streets with lethal coke which is 90% pure.

Deaths have soared in the past year, with dealers smuggling in triple-strength drugs from South America in a sick battle to offer the ‘best value’ coke on the high street.



Organised crime gangs are peddling a substance smuggled in from South America, and with Brits consuming the most cocaine in Europe, experts are warning that partygoers are dicing with death.

Drug charities and even plastic surgeons have reported a surge in cases of users struggling with the physical and mental toll of their cocaine use.



Speaking exclusively to The Sun Stacey Jordan, who lost her sister Lucy White, 24, in 2018, is giving an urgent warning about these drugs.

She said: “People don’t consider the consequences. Their mate could do it in a club one night and have a lovely night, so you think it will be fine, and you might do it and have a completely different experience.



“In Lucy’s case she did it on and off for 18 months and it caused a cardiac arrest. I think she liked the escapism it gave her after a difficult childhood, to try and fix problems, but after two days in hospital doctors told me she was brain dead.

“Even if she had have woken up, she would have been severely brain damaged. The effect on myself and my family has just been horrendous.

“I’ve never done drugs but people my age do it all the time and it’s something you come to accept because it’s just so out there.”

Experts warn that increasingly pure cocaine has fuelled a spike in British deaths, with people dying from cocaine rising by 15% in a year.



Traditional cocaine, with a purity level anywhere betwen 10 and 30% was known as ‘pub grub’ – three times weaker than the lethal drug now on offer, which can be 90%.

Once dubbed the ‘yuppie drug’ due to its popularity among executives and upper- class dinner party guests in the eighties, the drug claimed a record 1,279 lives in 2024, an increase of almost 15 per cent on the previous year, when 1,118 people died after taking it, according to the Office of National Statistics.

Professor of addiction at the University of York, Ian Hamilton, said: “It is clear the increasing purity of cocaine is a result of improved growing techniques and then more sophisticated processing techniques that transform raw coca into cocaine.

“Organised crime gangs are also becoming increasingly competitive with each other trying to provide more potent cocaine that represents better value to their customer base.

“This means cocaine is cheaper and stronger than it has ever been, this bucks the broader trend in the cost-of-living crisis that has seen most consumables going up in price.



“There are serious risks to health because of more potent cocaine availability. Whether you are an experienced or naïve user of cocaine the increased strength can catch people out. They have no way of knowing how strong the cocaine they are taking is until it is too late and they have ingested it.

“This is why we have seen increased fatal and non-fatal overdoses over the same time that cocaine strength increases. It is important for the government to intervene and sanction drug testing facilities so warnings about high strength cocaine can be given to people using the drug.”

Gangs selling cocaine typically cut the drug to increase profits, using a wide range of other substances like anaesthetics, caffeine, painkillers and amphetamines.



Harry Sumnall is a Professor in Substance Use at the Public Health Institute, Liverpool John Moores University. He said: “Despite levels of cocaine use remaining relatively stable in the general population, we are seeing record high levels of cocaine related deaths in England

and Wales.

“Treatment services have reported a sharp increase in people seeking support for their cocaine use, although many more people might be hesitant to seek support either due to stigma or not being aware of the help on offer.

“Despite the best efforts of police both here in the UK and internationally, cocaine has never been more affordable and more pure, and for those who want to take it, its readily available.

“We also know there’s a high level of harm in people who are mixing cocaine with alcohol. It’s therefore important that we increase efforts to reduce demand for cocaine, work on initiatives to reduce harm, and to make treatment services as welcoming as possible.”



Powdered cocaine, usually snorted or taken orally, can cause heart attacks, cardiac arrest, strokes and seizures, according to the NHS.

Mixing it with alcohol causes the liver to produce a highly toxic metabolite called coca ethylene, a chemical which stays in the body longer than either substance, and heightens the risk of medical effects on the heart, as well as seizures.

Today the drug is widely used among white and blue-collar sectors, and readily available to all ages, classes and ethnicities via WhatsApp, Snapchat and other social media apps.

Pre-covid a gram of the drug, also known as charlie, blow, sniff and marching powder, cost £100, but now is it as little as £50.



Brits use more cocaine than any other country in Europe, and the second most in the world, after Australia, according to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). It is the most commonly used drug in the UK, after cannabis, with around 20 per cent of that being ‘crack cocaine’, according to the government’s landmark Review of Drugs.

Users are mainly young adults. According to the ONS, 3.8 per cent of 16- to 24-year-olds took the drug in the year ending March 2024, compared with 2.1 per cent of people aged 16-59.

Mike Trace, who was appointed deputy drug tsar for Sir Tony Blair’s government and is now chief executive officer of the Forward Trust, a drug and alcohol support service, said: “I’m highly concerned we are observing higher purity in more places…and that’s where the death rate comes from.



“Higher, unpredictable purity is the biggest risk factor because if somebody buys white powder off their dealer on a Friday night and says, ‘right, well I generally think I get this much of a hit off that substance,’ and if they’re used to getting that much of a hit on 30 per cent pure substance, but if what they bought this Friday was 60 per

cent substance, they’re in trouble.”

GETTING HELP If you think that you have a drug addiction then please contact your GP. You can also visit FRANK for honest information about drugs and to find local treatment services. If you are having trouble finding the right help, call the FRANK drugs helpline on 0300 1236600. Or click here to visit the NHS website for more advice and support

Police forces in the UK routinely test seizures of drugs and send them off to be tested for purity. The National Crime Agency estimates the average purity at ‘user level’ was between 32 and 38 per cent in 2013.

Anonymous drugs investigations police source told The Sun: “All drugs seized are sent off for testing, and whereas a decade ago they were maybe 30 per cent pure, we’ve seen a sharp increase and even had up to 90 per cent pure.”

“We’ve seen a sharp increase of people coming to us for help with cocaine addiction,” said Abigail Wilson, Director of Pharmacy at We are With You drug and alcohol support charity.



“This is because it is becoming purer, cheaper and more socially acceptable. It used to be something you’d only see happening in a movie but now it’s becoming the normality for people to take in pubs, especially during national events like the World Cup.

“It’s also increasingly available online. The death rate is 11 times higher than in 2011, and the only way to address this is to teach people to use safely.

“We could say to people ‘say no to drugs’ and to not take them, but that doesn’t work.”



We are With You has shared advice on how to reduce risks when taking cocaine on their website.

The nation was shocked in the early 2000s when former EastEnders actress Danniella Westbrook was pictured with a missing septum, caused by years of cocaine addiction.

Dr Anil Joshi is a facial plastic surgeon who has seen an increase of people coming to him with signs of cocaine abuse.

He said: “When I examine patients, I can generally tell if they use cocaine. The first is the condition of the nasal lining. Instead of looking pink and healthy, it can be dry, sore and crusted. In some cases, ulcers bleed easily.

“Secondly, I often spot a literal hole in the septum, which is the wall separating the two nostrils. Cocaine can cause inflammation in the inner lining of the blood vessels that supply these areas, and therefore nourishment to these areas gets depleted and causes that region to necrose.



“The third is varying destruction of the nose. The septum and the sidewalls can lose their attachments and disappear altogether. This can result in creating a large cavity filled with thick secretions and crusts. This can produce a deeply unpleasant smell.

“The fourth is damage to the roof of the mouth or floor of the nasal cavity, thereby causing a hole between the nose and the mouth. This will severely affect eating and drinking, with food coming out through the nose, along with an extreme change in the tonality of speech. All of these can cause collapse of the midface, resulting in

gross disfigurement of the face.

“These signs are serious clues, not proof. I still have to rule out infection,

autoimmune and connective tissue disorders and cancers that cause similar damage.



“Pure cocaine is not cleaner in any meaningful sense. It can be more destructive because the same amount may contain a much larger dose. Street cocaine can also contain other chemicals. Some irritate the nose whilst others harm the immune system in a far more destructive way.

“The damage may not always be obvious at first. One may present to us with only mild congestion and a blocked nose, which can then progress to the loss of part of the septum, causing a hole that may whistle, form crusts, and bleed. I have regularly seen very severe cases in my clinic with total destruction of the nose and the face, and in some cases where it has progressed beyond repair.”

“I have received calls and then had to see them as emergencies when the situation has been both physical and psychological.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This is why I wish every young person could understand before they get tempted by their first line.

News.title: 8 bits of bad news snuck out in Keir Starmer's last week as Prime Minister from MI5 to birth rates
News.content:
8 bits of bad news snuck out in Keir Starmer's last week as Prime Minister from MI5 to birth rates

A grim list of threats the UK faces, new rules for MI5 chiefs, a police pay spat and alarming figures for school leaders have been released as the government takes out the trash before the summer break

View 4 Images The government has released a lot of news in the final days before the summer recess

The sun has nearly set on Keir Starmer's time as PM - but one time-honoured Westminster tradition lasted until the very end.

‌



In the last couple of days we've seen a flurry of government announcements as Parliament heads into its six-week summer break. These range from a run-down of the threats the country faces, an announcement over schools being affected by falling births and new rules for MI5 chiefs.

‌



Mr Starmer will depart No10 on Monday to be succeeded by Andy Burnham, who is expected to shake-up his top team.

‌



Here we look at some of the last-minute announcements that were slipped out before summer recess.

Loud fireworks to be banned outside professional displays to end 'nightmare' READ MORE :

Public thinks Nigel Farage battling with Count Binface to avoid scrutiny, poll finds READ MORE :

1. All the ways we're under threat

View 4 Images There was a grim warning about climate change and disease (Image: Getty Images)

One of the most grim statements we saw from a minister over the past couple of days was from key Starmer aide Darren Jones.

‌



The PM's chief secretary announced that a national resilience public awareness campaign will be launched this year. This will keep us informed of the multiple ways we're all under threat - from hostile states, deadly diseases and soaring temperatures.

The government has identified a total of 95 risks, his statement said. One bleak paragraph read: "As we saw with temperatures across the UK breaking records in May, only to be exceeded again in June, the risks we face from climate change cannot be underestimated, from our infrastructure, food and water systems or people’s immediate health.

"Climate change is also exacerbating the spread of high-consequence infectious diseases, alongside the changing boundaries of the human-animal interface. The incidence of highly pathogenic avian influenza, Ebola, and Andes hantavirus are examples from the last few months alone."

‌



Not the most cheery note to start the summer on.

2. Spat over police pay

Rank-and-file police officers have lashed out at the government after it announced a lower pay award than the figure recommended by an independent review body.

The Police Federation of England and Wales voiced its fury over a 3.5% rise announced on Wednesday. This was despite the Police Remuneration Review Body suggesting a 3.9% increase.

‌



Police Federation National Secretary John Partington said: "This is a pay rise on paper only, not in officers' pockets. In going against the advice of its own expert pay review body, the Home Office has sent a clear message to police officers that it will ignore the evidence that shows police officers are long overdue a pay award that reflects their service and sacrifice."

In a written statement Shabana Mahmood said: "The Government has given very careful consideration to the recommendations and has decided to award a consolidated increase of 3.5% to all ranks and pay points. This is the highest award that is manageable within existing police force and Home Office budgets, while enabling the continued delivery of the Government’s crime and policing priorities..."

3. Concerns about learning disability data

Disability rights experts reacted with concern after the Government slipped out changes to the way data is collected on people with learning disabilities this week.

‌



Grim stats from the annual Health and Care of People with Learning Disabilities report this week found that 78.8% of adults with Down syndrome died before the age of 65. And it said that the most common category of cause of death for autistic adults without a learning disability remains suicide, misadventure or accidental death.

But ministers also announced this will be the last Learning from Lives and Deaths of people with a learning disability and autistic people (LeDeR) report. Health minister Preet Kaur Gill said LeDeR data will be incorporated within a new patient level dataset to bring together, which she said will help better understand disparities.

Jon Sparkes OBE, chief executive of learning disability charity Mencap, said: “We urgently need to know how the Government will maintain independent scrutiny and, importantly, understand and tackle the causes of avoidable deaths. People with a learning disability need to know their lives are valued. Bereaved families need confidence lessons will be learned from their loved one’s death, and that other families will not have to face the same loss in future.”

‌



4. Huge MI5 failings leads to new measures

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood announced "decisive action" to deal with MI5 failings after it emerged chiefs knew an agent was a misogynist obsessed with violence.

Ms Mahmood unveiled a new package of measures to hold the Director General to account. It came after revelations about a neo-Nazi informant, known publicly as Agent X, who used his position to coercively control his girlfriend, including attacking her with a machete.

An investigation concluded MI5 gave false information to a court. Ms Mahmood said she would increase independent senior-level challenge and accountability of MI5’s internal reform and improvement programmes. She said: "MI5 plays a critical role in keeping our country, and the public, safe. I am deeply grateful for the commitment and dedication of its staff. However, given the significance of its responsibilities, it is imperative that the Service maintains the highest standards of integrity, accountability and rigour, particularly in its engagement with the courts.

‌



"This case demonstrates the damage to public, parliamentary and judicial confidence in our security services when MI5 gets it wrong."

View 4 Images Falling birth rates will cause problems for schools, Parliament was told (Image: South Wales Echo)

5. School fears over falling birth rates

The number of pupils in state-funded schools will plummet by more than 9% by 2031 due to falling birth rates, worrying stats released by the Department for Education showed on Thursday.

‌



Stats show the actual population in state-funded schools was 7,809,000 in 2026 but is projected to decrease by 726,000 (9.3%) by 2031.

Paul Whiteman, general secretary at school leaders’ union NAHT, raised concerns about school finances as funding is “heavily linked” to pupil numbers. “Falling school rolls are a real issue in many parts of the country due to declining birth rates,” he said.

“Where pupil intake is dwindling, this puts pressure on schools’ finances given that their funding is heavily linked to pupil numbers and their fixed staffing costs do not fall in line with numbers on roll. This can affect their ability to support existing staffing and curriculum breadth, and potentially affect their long-term viability, with small and rural schools especially vulnerable.”

‌



6. Fury over aid cuts for Africa

Ministers have been accused of “abandoning” some of the world’s poorest countries after announcing major cuts to aid spending in Africa.

Plans published on Thursday will see regional aid spending slashed by 42% over the next three years, equivalent to more than £1 billion. Spending on aid to Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique and Malawi is set to fall by 90% or more, reaching just £5 million each by 2029.

Other African countries expected to suffer significant cuts include Ghana (52%), Rwanda (82%), Sierra Leone (69%), Zambia (83%) and Zimbabwe (72%).

‌



Aid network Bond said the cuts represented a “shredding of decades long partnerships and programmes” and warned the UK was “ceding it’s leadership and role across the continent”.

Spending on Somalia, Syria and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is expected to fall by more than a third.

7. More work needed on fraud

On Tuesday independent reviewer Jonathan Fisher released a report on the way the UK handles online fraud. This warned that fraud now accounts for half of all surveyed crime, and called for more work to be done in a "decisive shift in posture".

‌



It said the current system is reactive, but there must be more proactive work to improve work with the private sector and data sharing. The document made 47 recommendations, which ministers are considering.

Responding to the report, Security Minister Dame Angela Eagle wrote: "The report’s recommendations cut across the responsibilities of multiple departments, agencies and sectors. The Government will now consider them carefully and will respond in due course.

"Tackling fraud requires sustained collaboration between Government, law enforcement, regulators, industry and civil society. This Government is determined to build momentum in the fight against fraud: to support victims, to pursue those who profit from deception, to strengthen deterrence, and to make the UK a safer place to live, work and do business."

‌



View 4 Images Steve Reed faced anger in the Commons over council plans (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

8. Backlash over shake-up of councils

Local Government Secretary Steve Reed faced fury from some of his own MPs after confirming the details of a major shake-up of local councils. There's debate over whether this one is bad news or not, but it's certainly a controversial policy - and has sparked anger on the Labour benches.

On the final day of Parliament before the summer recess, he announced that a reorganisation of local councils in England “will have cut the number of councils from 317 to a maximum of 173” in England.

Article continues below

During a Commons Statement on Friday, Mr Reed said: “This Government is driving the most ambitious programme of local government reform in a generation, replacing the inefficient two-tier system with new unitary councils so that all parts of our country are ready for devolution."

But he faced anger from MPs across parties - including from his own benches. Labour MP for Gedling Michael Payne asked Mr Reed “what on earth” made sense for his area in Nottingham, while Labour MP for Burnley Oliver Ryan said he was “so angry” with proposals to create an East Lancashire local authority, which he said could be one of the poorest in the country.

News.title: Aberdeen University worker charged after making online post 'wishing Ann Widdecombe a painful death'
News.content:
Aberdeen University worker charged after making online post 'wishing Ann Widdecombe a painful death'

Heather Herbert, 50, a web developer at Aberdeen University, has been charged in relation to posts on Bluesky made before it emerged that Ms Widdecombe's death was being investigated as murder

View 4 Images Heather Herbert, 50, has been charged by police in connection to social media posts she allegedly made about Ms Widdecombe (Image: Heather Herbert/Facebook)

A university worker has been charged by police after being accused of wishing Ann Widdecombe "an extremely painful death".

‌



Heather Herbert, 50, is accused of posting the comment on social media, where she also allegedly claimed it was "good news" the former Cabinet Minister had died, adding she hoped she was "handcuffed to the bed as she screamed in agony”.

‌



The posts were allegedly published on Bluesky last week before it was announced that Ms Widdecombe’s death at her Dartmoor home was being treated as murder. Police Scotland had previously said the comments contained "no criminality”, before announcing on Thursday that they had charged Herbert with an offence.

‌



View 4 Images Ann Widdecombe was found dead in the kitchen of her home in Haytor, Devon, last Thursday (Image: Christopher Jones/Shutterstock)

Details of the charge will be made public at Herbert’s first court appearance. A spokesman for the force said: "We received reports on Saturday 11 July 2026 relating to a post made online. Following further assessment, a 50-year-old has been arrested and charged in connection. A report will be submitted to the procurator fiscal.”

Aberdeen University, where Ms Herbert works as a web developer, is also looking into the comments. Principal and Vice Chancellor, Professor Peter Edwards, said earlier this week the university has a zero-tolerance approach to "violence or hateful behaviour", and gave his assurance the comments were being investigated "as a priority".

‌



A spokesman added: "The comments that have been shared are entirely the individual’s own and do not represent the views of the [university]. We do not condone violence or hateful behaviour in any form. We are co-operating with Police Scotland as they carry out their inquiries and cannot comment further.”

View 4 Images Ms Widdecombe lived in an isolated cottage with her cat in Devon (Image: Getty Images)

The Scottish Greens are also said to be looking into the comments. Ms Herbert joined the Scottish Greens in late 2021 after previously being a member of Scottish Labour.

‌



Ms Widdecombe was found dead in her home in Haytor, Devon, last Thursday aged 78. The veteran politician, who was also briefly a Brexit Party MEP before becoming a Reform UK spokesperson, is believed to have lay dead in her cottage’s kitchen for 24 hours before she was found.

A 28-year-old suspect, from Rotherham, South Yorks, was arrested on suspicion of Ms Widdecombe's murder on Saturday and is still being questioned. The man, who cannot be named, was re-arrested on Monday accused of commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism, and as a result he could be held for up to seven days without charge while police carry out their investigations.

View 4 Images Liz Truss speaking on stage at the CPAC GB event in London on Thursday morning (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

The Police Scotland announcement came just hours after former Prime Minister and Conservative Party leader Liz Truss, 50, broke down in tears on stage as she led a tribute to Ann Widdecombe during a speech in London. Speaking about the former Tory MP, at the Conservative Political Action Conference GB, Ms Truss said: “Before we start on this conference, I'd like to take time to pay our respects to the late Ann Widdecombe, who was brutally murdered in her home last week."

She added: “I've known Ann for over 20 years. She was a deeply principled politician who stood for the very values we are fighting for at CPAC: free speech, patriotism and the family. She was courageous and fearless in standing up to the leftist drift we have seen in Britain. She was a kind and generous human being, and we are all so devastated that she has been taken from us. Now let's reflect on Ann's remarkable life."

News.title: Mum guilty of killing 3-month-old baby after exposing her to heat from hairdryer
News.content:
Mum guilty of killing 3-month-old baby after exposing her to heat from hairdryer

Courtney Gartshore, 28, has been found guilty of killing her three-month-old daughter Dahlia-Rose Gartshore, who suffered serious burns after being exposed to heat from a hairdryer

View 2 Images Three-month-old Dahlia-Rose Gartshore was exposed to heat from a hairdryer (Image: Police Handout)

A mum has been found guilty of killing her three-month-old daughter after exposing her to heat from a hairdryer.

‌



Courtney Gartshore, 28, had denied culpable homicide of her three-month-old daughter Dahlia-Rose who was in her care in Peterhead, Aberdeenshire, in September 2023.

‌



Jurors took just over an hour to reach a guilty verdict on the seventh day of the trial at the High Court in Aberdeen. Gartshore sobbed as she was led from the dock to the cells, BBC reports.

‌



She was found guilty of culpably and recklessly causing Dahlia-Rose to be subjected to heat from the appliance while the child was in her sole care. The charge stated Dahlia-Rose's injuries were so severe that she died as a result.

Gartshore is due to be sentenced at the High Court in Edinburgh on August 14.

‌



View 2 Images Courtney Gartshore (Image: Police Handout)

Jurors heard that Dahlia-Rose suffered burns to 18% of her body and that her DNA was found on the hairdryer.

A recording of the 999 call made by Gartshore during which she told dispatchers her child had gone "purple" while asleep was played to jurors.

Article continues below

Expert witness and burns specialist Dr Timothy Burges told the court that it was his view the heat injuries did not cause Dahlia-Rose's death, and that she could have already been dead.

The court heard allegations that Gartshore had consumed alcohol before the child's death. Other charges she had originally faced were dropped by the Crown before the case went to the jury.

News.title: FIFA charge £60 for World Cup final press conference place alongside Rio Ferdinand
News.content:
FIFA charge £60 for World Cup final press conference place alongside Rio Ferdinand

Fans will need to dig deep into their pockets for the chance to attend a press conference with the former Manchester United defender

View 2 Images Rio Ferdinand will make an appearance at the FIFA World Cup final press conference

World Cup fans will be charged £60 a head to attend a press conference involving finalists Argentina and Spain, as well as Manchester United icon Rio Ferdinand. FIFA have linked up with the global sports retailer Fanatics, its commercial partner, to host a fan festival at the Javits Centre in New York City on Friday.

‌



Hundreds of fans will be granted access to the press conference, which takes place two days before Sunday's final at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. However, they will have to pay a hefty price to have the privilege of gaining access.

‌



Ferdinand will be hosting the press conference event, which features an appearance from FIFA president Gianni Infantino as a 'special guest'. But rather than invite fans to the one-off event for free, FIFA will be cashing in by charging £60 per head.

‌



A Fanatics advert read: "Fans will have the rare opportunity to see both finalists take the stage just days before the World Cup final, hearing directly from players and team representatives as they prepare for sport's biggest match. Special guests: Gianni Infantino and more coming soon."

Fans who want to commemorate the occasion with an official photograph alongside Ferdinand will be forced to shell out £100. While FIFA are handling the press conference itself, access will be granted to those who have paid for their Fanatics Fest ticket.

England miss out on £18m payday immediately after Argentina heartbreak READ MORE :

According to The Times, the American organisation said the entry fee covers numerous events across many different sports with athletes including LeBron James, Novak Djokovic, Tom Brady, Serena Williams, Sir David Beckham and others.

‌



Ferdinand's growing influence within FIFA has not gone unnoticed. The 47-year-old was one of few former footballers to publicly back FIFA's approach to the Folarin Balogun ban controversy - though he did later admit it was the wrong decision - and hosted the World Cup draw for the expanded 48-team group stage back in December.

The ex-England international is one of dozens of former footballers who represents the world football governing body on a global stage. Like many past footballers, Ferdinand operates as a 'FIFA legend' in an ambassadorial-type role for promotional events similar to the Fanatics one.

View 2 Images Rio Ferdinand is classified as a 'FIFA legend' at promotional events (Image: Michael Regan - FIFA, FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The chance to meet Ferdinand is not even the most expensive opportunity available for fans to purchase, though. The price varies based on which star athlete is featured in the photo, with a memento including former MLB star Alex Rodriguez costing a whopping £239 for a photo.

Ferdinand's absence from the pundit studio for both BBC and ITV has been noted, with the ex-England defender choosing to cover the tournament via his YouTube channel 'Rio Ferdinand Presents'. He also posted a social media video of himself celebrating England's opening goal in the 2-1 defeat to Argentina on Wednesday.
