He is not the most physically imposing player and does not zip about the pitch with great intensity, with his 53.7 pressures per 90 putting him behind 63 other midfielders last season. United probably still need to sign a powerful runner to ease worries about being caught in transition, but he tends to win his individual battles on the pitch: only three regular midfielders in the league last season had a better win rate in duels (62%).

Tielemans is 29 so very much a player for the present but Santos, just 22, has plenty of potential to develop. After returning from a promising loan spell at Strasbourg – where he thrived in a box-to-box role and was voted in the Ligue 1 team of the season for 2024-25 – dislodging Enzo Fernández and Moisés Caicedo in the Chelsea midfield was always going to be tough. He may not have been the player United fans expected to sign this season, but he looks like a smart, considered acquisition who may prove something of a coup for Carrick.

This is an article by Opta Analyst

Sports.title: Championship club finally agree deal to buy £27m stadium after playing in it for two decades
Sports.content:
Championship club finally agree deal to buy £27m stadium after playing in it for two decades

Swansea City have agreed to buy the Swansea.com Stadium from the local council, 21 years after they moved into the ground.

The Swans first played at the 21,088-capacity venue, formerly known as the Liberty Stadium, in 2005.

2 Swansea are set to have ownership of their stadium Credit: Getty

Swansea Council built the stadium for a reported £27million and have owned it since then.

However, ownership is now set to be transferred to the Championship club, who have had operational control for eight years.

According to council leader Rob Stewart via the BBC, the stadium sale price will exceed a 'fair open-market value'.

It is also said that Swansea believe their acquisition will allow them to generate more income and draw in further investment.

Major step for Swansea

Top of the club's ownership structure with a 71.18 per cent stake are Swansea Football LLC, controlled by Brett Cravatt and Jason Cohen.

British businessman Nigel Morris owns 12.9 per cent, whilst Swansea City Supporters Society Ltd have another 6.98 per cent.

Ballon d'Or winner Luka Modric is also part of the ownership group, as well as rap legend Snoop Dogg, who modelled last season's home kit.

Swansea's owners want to secure promotion back to the Premier League, which they last featured in during the 2017/18 campaign.

"It's very difficult for them (the club) to do that if they're not in control of the asset," said Stewart.

The purchase of their stadium marks a significant boost towards that goal as they head into a ninth consecutive Championship season.

2 Swansea have played at their home ground for over two decades Credit: Getty

Swansea's Premier League wait goes on

Following relegation from the top flight in 2018, Swansea have come close to returning on two occasions.

They reached the Championship play-offs in 2020 and 2021, but lost in the respective semi-finals and final.

Since then, they have only finished as high as tenth in the second tier, with 11th being their final standing for last season.

Swansea's hopes of promotion will be boosted in the new season due to the introduction of two extra play-off places.

Teams finishing third to sixth normally enter the play-offs, but now seventh and eighth will also be involved.

Third and fourth enter the semi-finals, whilst fifth face eighth and sixth take on seventh in one-match eliminators to reach the last four.

Sports.title: EFL defender ruled out for ‘majority of season’ just three weeks after joining new club
Sports.content:
EFL defender ruled out for ‘majority of season’ just three weeks after joining new club

Oxford United have confirmed summer signing Frankie Kent is set to miss the 'majority of the season' through injury.

The defender has undergone surgery on an anterior cruciate ligament injury suffered in pre-season training.

3 Kent has been ruled out for the 'majority of the season' after knee surgery Credit: Getty

It comes just three weeks after Kent joined the club from Hearts.

The 30-year-old was signed on a free transfer back on June 27 by the League One club.

However, he will not make his competitive debut until at least 2027 following the injury setback.

Oxford statement

Oxford revealed the extent of his lay-off in a club statement on Thursday.

The U's said: "Oxford United can confirm that Frankie Kent has undergone successful surgery after sustaining an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

"Kent sustained the injury during a training session and is expected to miss the majority of the 2026/27 season.

"The defender joined the Club this summer following three years with Heart of Midlothian.

"He will now begin the rehabilitation phase of his recovery under the care of the Club's medical staff.

"Everyone at Oxford United wishes Frankie a full and speedy recovery, and the entire Club will support him every step of the way."

Kent was part of the Hearts side which finished second in the Scottish Premiership last season.

3 Oxford completed the signing of Kent from Hearts on June 27 Credit: Getty

He made 95 appearances in all competitions during three years with the Jambos.

The former Arsenal academy starlet has also had spells with Colchester United and Peterborough United.

Latest setback

His new club have now been dealt a significant blow ahead of their return to the third-tier.

Oxford were relegated last season following two seasons in the Championship.

Aaron Ramsey has since been appointed as manager, replacing Matt Bloomfield in the dugout.

However, his side are currently blocked from making new signings due to an EFL transfer embargo.

3 Oxford boss Ramsey will be without his new signing until at least the new year Credit: Instagram @oufcofficial

Oxford begin their league campaign at home to MK Dons on August 15.

It comes a week after their Carabao Cup first round tie away to Leyton Orient.

Sports.title: Harry Kane ends 40-year World Cup streak after England crash out with a whimper
Sports.content:
Harry Kane ends 40-year World Cup streak after England crash out with a whimper

England's World Cup exit has ended Bayern Munich's stunning 40-year streak of having at least one squad player in every final.

Skipper Harry Kane failed to inspire the Three Lions to reach a first World Cup final since 1966 as Thomas Tuchel's side lost 2-1 to Argentina in Wednesday's semi-final.



2 Kane could have played in his final World Cup game for England Credit: Getty

England were just five minutes of normal time away from setting up a final meeting with Spain on Sunday following Anthony Gordon's 55th minute opener.

But holders Argentina equalised through Enzo Fernandez's strike from range in the 85th minute, before Lautaro Martinez headed home a stoppage-time winner.

Argentina now have the chance to become the first nation since Brazil in 1962 to retain the title.



England's heartbreak has seen many fans and pundits demand Tuchel leave the dugout following his decision to shut up shop immediately after England's opener.

talkSPORT understands that the FA have no plans to sack him with the German having a contract through to Euro 2028.



Waving Good-Bay to history

While England's 60-year trophy drought continues, their defeat to Argentina has finally put an end to Bayern's 40-year streak, which spanned across 11 editions.

From 1982 to 2022, the Bavarian giants had at least one player competing for the biggest trophy in world football.



Kane was the only player on Bayern's books in the England squad.

Meanwhile in the other semi-final, Spain overcome France 2-0 as they advanced into their first World Cup final since winning the tournament in 2010.

Bayern had two representatives in the Les Bleus squad - winger Michael Olise and centre-back Dayot Upamecano.

Bayern Munich's 40-year World Cup final streak 1982 final - Italy 3-1 West Germany West Germany: Paul Breitner, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, Wolfgang Dremmle 1986 final - Argentina 3-2 West Germany West Germany: Lothar Matthaus, Dieter Hoeness, Norbert Eder 1990 final - West Germany 1-0 Argentina West Germany: Klaus Augenthaler, Stefan Reuter, Jurgen Kohler 1994 final - Brazil 0-0 Italy (3-2 on penalties) Brazil: Jorginho 1998 final - France 3-0 Brazil France: Bixente Lizarazu 2002 final - Brazil 2-0 Germany Germany: Oliver Kahn, Thomas Linke, Jens Jeremies 2006 final - Italy 1-1 France (5-3 on penalties) France: Willy Sagnol 2010 final - Spain 1-0 Netherlands Netherlands: Mark van Bommel, Arjen Robben, Edson Braafheid 2014 final - Germany 1-0 Argentina Germany: Philipp Lahm, Toni Kroos, Thomas Muller, Mario Gotze, Bastian Schweinsteiger, Jerome Boateng, Manuel Neuer 2018 final - France 4-2 Croatia France: Corentin Tolisso 2022 final - Argentina 3-3 France (4-2 on penalties) France: Dayot Upamecano, Benjamin Pavard, Kingsley Coman

Will Harry Kane play in the 2030 World Cup?

In the immediate aftermath of England's exit, attention has turned to whether Kane may have played his final World Cup match.

The 32-year-old, who was given a 6/10 in Adrian Durham's player ratings against Argentina, finished as England's joint top scorer alongside Jude Bellingham with six goals in North America.



Having become England's most capped outfield player in history on Wednesday, he also leaves the World Cup as his country's outright top scorer in the competition.

But the centre forward has admitted he is unsure whether he will be continuing to write his name in World Cup history in four years time, with the player to be 36 when it next rolls around.

He said: "It’s still too early to say. I take it year by year and see how I feel.

“I love playing for England. But of course, four years is a long time.



2 Kane's six World Cup goals in North America have brought his tally to 14 across three tournaments

"Then again, you can see someone like [Lionel] Messi still performing at the highest level even at an older age.

“I honestly don’t know. Right now, I just need to process this elimination.

"We gave everything we had, but in the end, it wasn’t enough.”

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League referee reveals ‘irritating’ Harry Kane behaviour turns officials against him
Sports.content:
Former Premier League referee Graham Scott has opened up about some of Harry Kane's 'irritating' behaviour on the pitch.

Scott was a guest on talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Jacobs the morning after England's painful World Cup semi-final exit to Argentina.

2 England suffered World Cup semi-final heartbreak for the third time since 1966 Credit: Getty

As anticipated, the two great rivals gave referee Ismael Elfath plenty to keep on top of, with tensions threatening to boil over on a few occasions in Atlanta.

Argentina came from a goal down to triumph 2-1 and set up a mouthwatering World Cup final showdown with Spain on Sunday, while England head into the dreaded third place play-off against France on Saturday.

'It just annoys you'

In the end, only one England player was booked – Elliot Anderson – but Scott expressed his disappointment about the Three Lions' players 'chipping away' at the man in the middle.

"It really annoys me watching our players trying to chip away at the ref because that's not going to work," Scott said.

"I've been on the receiving end of it from these people.

"It just annoys you [as a referee]. It doesn't get you what you want [as a player]. It doesn't achieve what you're hoping it will achieve.

"And, well, the Argentinians seem rather more effective at it – so what can we learn from that?

"It's also understanding about how different referees operate. So, do we actually watch the ref? Do we analyse them before the game? Do we think, 'Right, he's going to let this go'?

"We [referees] can exploit that as well, potentially, but also, be ready for that onslaught because it's coming."

Scott explained his frustration at England players' behaviour towards the referee and gave particular insight into what it's like to officiate Kane – as he did during his 10 years as a Premier League official.

"He's very repetitive," Scott continued. "And it is the sarcastic leading question of 'Is he going to be allowed to do that all day? Are you going to give us anything? Do you know there are two teams out here...?'. And it just irritates you.

2 Ismael Elfath largely kept his cards in his pocket during England's 2-1 loss to Argentina Credit: AFP

"[I used to think], 'I wish you'd just go away' and then... if anything, when the 50-50 call comes in, 'No, you're not getting it, because I've taken against you as a person now'.

"It doesn't work, Harry, and I'd love to speak to him about it because he could be effective, sure, but what he's trying now doesn't work.

"And I've seen it in the Premier League, of course. I don't know what he's always like in the Bundesliga – I've not watched it – but it is frustrating...

'They're not unpleasant people'

"And it looks like [Jude] Bellingham follows a similar pattern. The only time I refereed him was when he was at Birmingham as a kid, so ... he would have changed a lot since then."

Bellingham was involved in a heated exchange with Lionel Messi on Wednesday night.

Scott did have praise for both Kane and Bellingham, though, the latter of whom has been tipped to succeed the former as England captain.

"In so many ways, they're such great role models, don't get me wrong" he emphasised. "And they're not unpleasant people, but it's about what works.

"And I do think when it comes to referees, people haven't really thought about what works with refs to get them on your side – and all we ever do is rinse and repeat, berate, batter, shout [in the hope] eventually they'll buckle.

"Well, if everyone's doing it, I suppose it evens itself out."

Sports.title: Arsenal agree deal to sign Leandro Trossard replacement in record-breaking transfer
Sports.content:
Arsenal have agreed a deal to sign Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge in a deal worth £34million, talkSPORT understands.

The 24-year-old is having his move to the Gunners formalised after talks accelerated on Thursday, following the departure of cult hero Leandro Trossard to Besiktas in a £17m deal.



3 Tzolis is set to make the move to Arsenal to end his two-year spell in Belgium Credit: Getty

Should the transfer be completed, it would make Tzolis the most expensive Greek player of all time - eclipsing the £31.4m fee Brighton paid to sign Charalampos Kostoulas from Olympiacos last summer.

And the winger is also set to become the most expensive sale in Belgian Pro League history - breaking a four-year record.

Charles De Ketelaere has been the record departure as a result of his £29.7m move from Brugge to AC Milan.



Going Tzol in

Mikel Arteta will be hoping Tzolis will be able to replicate Trossard's goalscoring exploits from the left wing.

During the 31-year-old forward's three-and-a-half-year stint in north London, he chipped in with 36 goals and 34 assists in 174 games across all competitions.



But Tzolis has shown he has an eye for goal since joining Brugge in 2024 from Norwich City.

In his first season in Belgium, he found the back of the net 21 times from 56 matches.



And the 2025/26 campaign proved to be his most successful to date as he chipped in with 22 goals and 29 assists from 52 games - firing Brugge to the league title.

Only Bayern Munich duo Harry Kane [68] and Michael Olise [54] registered more goal involvements than Tzolis' 51 in world football.

In total for Brugge, he has scored 43 goals and provided 45 assists in 108 appearances across his two years there.

3 Tzolis is being signed by Arsenal to replace Trossard, who has joined Besiktas Credit: Getty



3 He scored three goals in 30 matches during his time at Norwich Credit: Getty

Heading back to England

Tzolis has experience of playing in England, having been on Norwich's books between 2021-2024 - a spell which saw him shipped off on loan twice to FC Twente and Fortuna Dusseldorf.

Ironically, the 34-cap Greece international made his Premier League debut against Arsenal at the Emirates in September 2021.

That game was one of 14 top-flight outings Tzolis made for the Canaries, with the player failing to chip in with a single goal involvement.



But he has found his shooting boots since departing Carrow Road - starting with his initial loan spell at Dusseldorf in the 2023/24 term - where he scored on 24 occasions.

Who else have Arsenal been linked with?

talkSPORT understands that Aston Villa star Morgan Rogers is Arsenal's top target this window.

And the deal for Tzolis is separate from the pursuit of Rogers.

The Gunners are also keen to sign Newcastle skipper Bruno Guimaraes, though the two clubs differ regarding the Brazilian's valuation.

Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez is another player that is admired by Arsenal, while Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola has also been linked.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel’s comments on ex-England manager Gareth Southgate and Euro 2024 come back to haunt him
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel’s comments on ex-England manager Gareth Southgate and Euro 2024 come back to haunt him

Just last year, Thomas Tuchel criticised England and Gareth Southgate for being afraid of elimination from Euro 2024.

Now, that stance has majorly come back to bite the Three Lions boss, as his own side exited the World Cup with a whimper.



3 Tuchel has become a culprit of the exact same thing he wanted to change Credit: Getty

Tuchel had taken issue with Southgate's negative tactics and the team's identity when reviewing their campaign at the Euros.

Soon after his appointment, in March 2025, he was asked by ITV: "Yes or no, did England have a clear playing style last summer?"

To which the German simply replied: "Not last summer, no."

And after being asked to explain what was missing, he continued: "The identity, the clarity, the rhythm, the repetition of patterns, the freedom of the players, the expression, the hunger.



"They were more afraid to drop out of the tournament, in my observation, than having the excitement and hunger to win it."

But just over a year later, Tuchel's comments have backfired, with England seemingly ditching their hunger to win.



The Three Lions manager has been slammed, with some saying he should be sacked for his negative approach to the heartbreaking 2-1 semi-final defeat to Argentina on Wednesday night.

After Anthony Gordon gave his nation the lead, Tuchel soon brought on Ezri Konsa, with England sitting back to defend.



He then went on to bring on Dan Burn and Nico O'Reilly, as his side dropped deeper and deeper, looking to see their lead out.

But it didn't go as planned, as Argentina would go on to pile an incredible amount of pressure on England, who eventually caved in the 85th minute, with Enzo Fernandez smashing home.

3 Tuchel had criticised England and Southgate for their negative approach at Euro 2024 Credit: Getty

Lautaro Martinez then headed in in stoppage time to complete a late turnaround and sink the Three Lions' hopes and dreams.



Shockingly, in the time between Gordon's opener and Martinez's winner, Tuchel's men had just 12 per cent possession.

That indicated just how much they sat back to defend for their lives in the final stages of the semi-final, which was something unexpected from Tuchel considering his past words on Southgate.

'Nonsensical' approach

As part of a scathing assessment of Tuchel's tactics, talkSPORT's Paul Hawksbee reminded listeners of his 2025 comments.

He said on Hawksbee and Jacobs on Thursday: "What he said in March about Gareth Southgate, semi-trashing the legacy of the guy who got us far in tournaments...



"Did we have the 'excitement and hunger' to win it?

3 Tuchel watched on as his side succumbed to the immense pressure they invited on Credit: Getty

"It looks like he froze and decided to do what we did against Mexico, which was nonsensical against a team like Argentina."

He added: "What was he trying to do? That's what happens when you play like a League One team that has gone 1-0 up in the FA Cup against Man United.

"You look at the substitutions and the players must think: 'Is that it, gaffer? Is that our ambition? To park on the edge of the box'."



Tuchel defended his decisions when speaking post-match, saying: "If it doesn't go well, it's easy to say I was wrong."

But that will leave fans frustrated after seeing the manager appear to go against the very thing he didn't want to see England do.

The FA are understood to currently have no plans to sack Tuchel, amid calls for Pep Guardiola or Eddie Howe to be approached.

Sports.title: Chicago pours $424m into stadium project with $195bn giant that will be first of its kind in US
Sports.content:
The Chicago Fire's new stadium is privately funded but local lawmakers are expected to chip in for surrounding infrastructure.

Chicago pours $424m into stadium project with $195bn giant that will be first of its kind in US

The Chicago Bears have been forced to leave the Windy City to land public funds, but the Fire have been more fortunate.

NFL fans could soon be streaming over the boarder to Indiana as the franchise packs its bags and leaves Soldier Field for a dome.



4 The Fire's latest renders revealed McDonald's as a sponsor Credit: Chicago Fire FC / Gensler

Soccer is staying put, however, with MLS' Fire picking a downtown site to lay down roots.

The Chicago Tribune's Brian J. Rogal reports that Chicago City Council’s Finance Committee voted to devote $424 million in property tax revenue toward infrastructure.

Pending approval from the full council, the money will help pay for new roads and pedestrian walkways.



The $750 million stadium, being built at The 78, is being privately financed.

Per the report, the developer Related Midwest will get “reimbursed for building new roads that link the vacant former rail yard to surrounding neighborhoods, along with a walkable riverfront and other pedestrian walkways.”



A “city-owned, 1,200-space parking garage and a public plaza above it” is reportedly the most expensive addition, covering around half of the outlay.

The Fire broke ground in March and hope to move in for the 2028 season.



Infrastructure work is not expected to be completed for another three years after the stadium opens.

Chicago Fire and McDonald's announce stadium partnership

The 22,000-seater arena is set to be called McDonald’s Park.

It is the first time the fast food giant, which boasts a market capitalization of $191 billion per Yahoo Finance, has been a naming-rights partner for a U.S. sports franchise.

4 The stadium is not being paid for from the public purse Credit: Chicago Fire FC / Gensler

4 Fans will be able to visit the golden arches at games Credit: Chicago Fire FC / Gensler



A permanent flagship location will be based within the concourse.

“As we take the next step on our journey to build a world class club, our commitment to Chicago is at the center of everything we do,” Fire owner Joe Mansueto said in a statement. “That’s why McDonald’s is the perfect partner – an iconic global brand with deep Chicago roots and shared values in supporting our community.

"McDonald’s Park will be the stadium that Chicago deserves.”

The Fire currently play at Soldier Field, which is in need of an overhaul.

A proposal has been put forward to spend a massive $630 million turning the ancient arena into a world-class entertainment venue.

“It’s time for new audiovisual. Also, if the Bears leave, we have to rework the back of the house spaces they use for their offices, their locker rooms,” Chicago Park District leader Carlos Ramirez-Rosa told NBC5 Chicago.



4 New walkways and roads will be built Credit: Chicago Fire FC / Gensler

“$500 million of the $630 million is for ingress and egress, improving the ways that people get in and out of Soldier Field, making it easier for people to enjoy concerts there.”

“Soldier Field is a public asset, and so we want to make sure we’re taking care of that asset because it generates major revenue," Ramirez-Rosa added. "It creates good jobs. It’s an engine for the local tourism economy.

"Ultimately, we want to keep the Bears in Chicago, but we have to be prepared for any circumstance that may occur."



Stay up to date on all things NFL across our talkSPORT platforms - subscribe to our YouTube channel for the latest news, opinion, exclusive interviews and our daily unfiltered, unscripted show 'The S* Word, from 8am ET.

Sports.title: Simon Jordan: Hypocrite Thomas Tuchel should be fired as England manager and apologise to players
Sports.content:
talkSPORT's Simon Jordan has launched a scathing attack on under-fire England boss Thomas Tuchel.

Tuchel's defensive tactics have been called into question after the Three Lions crashed out of the World Cup semi-finals to Argentina.



4 Tuchel's tactical decisions in the later stages of the game backfired badly Credit: Getty

England led until the 85th minute in Atlanta through Anthony Gordon's deadlock-breaking goal, only to sit back and invite pressure which eventually paid.

Enzo Fernandez fired in a stunning equaliser from outside the box before Lautaro Martinez completed the turnaround in stoppage time, with Lionel Messi setting up both goals.

And after seeing England throw away their shot at a first World Cup final since 1966, Jordan insists Tuchel has to go.



'It's an embarrassment'

The former Crystal Palace chairman had previously been a fierce advocate for Tuchel, believing his 'winning mentality' could take England where Gareth Southgate couldn't.

But Jordan was forced to admit that Tuchel debunked his theory at the first opportunity.



Asked if England were international football's greatest 'nearly men', he said: "It's an embarrassment, isn't it. It's actually an embarrassment to British football, to English football.

"We've got this huge ego about our league. We create this song that we live and die by that constantly gets trotted out. We turn up in tournaments and we don't win.



"The Greeks won the 2004 Euros. Everybody seems to win something. The French have built teams and when they get to semi-finals and finals and lose them, they come back and win the next version of it. We don't.

"We had everything in our favour. We had a favourable group; we had decent draws like Southgate got. We got Norway rather than one of the other sides; we got Argentina rather than Spain or France. We got it all in our camp. It had nothing to do with bad decisions or bad referees, lack of fortune. This was just a bad performance from the manager."

Jordan is not the only pundit fuming in the wake of England's underwhelming second-half display, with calls growing for the FA to sound out Pep Guardiola.

4 Tuchel took over as England manager at the start of last year Credit: AFP



Responding to the question of whether Tuchel should stay in charge, as talkSPORT understands he is expected to do, Jordan continued: "No. I think the FA should fire him. I know it's very reactionary.

"I think it was ridiculous of them giving him a job post-tournament [Tuchel extended his contract until Euro 2028] prior to the tournament.

"I think his sole focus in life was to get into the mainstay of the tournament. The opportunity was there. This Argentina side are not mugs, but they're not world-beaters. Messi is a fabulous player; he's gone from a winger now to a No.10 who can do what he wants. He's a fabulous player, but by Christ did we help him and make it easy for the Argentinians.

"I think there's more reasons not to have Tuchel going into Euro 2028. He's a hypocrite.



"First of all, he doesn't do what he says he's going to do. Second of all, he clearly doesn't believe in the side. Third of all, he makes tactical decisions... When it comes on top, you get one moment in life; you get one opportunity to create a first impression. If it's there, you've got to take it; you've got to make it.

"His opportunity was to change the way the team was setting up in the second half and he didn't do it. That to me means there's something missing in the capability of Tuchel at this level.

4 England have lost all three of their World Cup semi-finals since they lifted the trophy in 1966 Credit: Getty

"I think there are more reasons to not have Tuchel than to keep him in."



England players 'owed an apology'

Jordan went as far to suggest Tuchel should apologise to the players, adding: "Listen, you'll never hear me say this very often: I think the players are owed an apology by the manager [for] the decisions that he made, because I think he let the players down.

"I think some of the things he has said, I applauded. But when I look back at them, I think, 'Well, that's wonderful you said them, but I'm not sure what you created by doing it'."

A stunned White replied: "My god, I've never heard you say that before, Simon."

Case for the defence

Ex-England captain Stuart Pearce also weighed in on the furore surrounding Tuchel. He told White and Jordan after the game: "Listen, I can't defend some of the substitutions he made. There's no doubt about it, all it did was bring Argentina onto us.



"To be honest, in a game that we lost by the odd goal, they hit our post twice and [Jordan] Pickford made an outstanding save, so it could have been a lot worse than it actually was, let's make no mistake about that.

4 It's another bitter World Cup defeat for England as their 60-year trophy drought continues

"I'm not defending the performance, but if you make a change now, I'm defending the making of the change. I don't see where we go and what direction we go from there.

"We're scratching our heads tomorrow morning if Thomas Tuchel gets sacked and then we go from there. That's the problem we've got. Then we send another experienced manager who is potentially a rookie at major tournaments. That, for me, is a dangerous thing to do."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel has got to find a way to get the best out of his top technical talent ahead of Euro 2028. No other country in the world would leave Phil Foden, Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold at home, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has got to find a way to get the best out of his top technical talent ahead of Euro 2028. No other country in the world would leave Phil Foden, Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold at home, writes IAN LADYMAN

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

With Thomas Tuchel’s bid to put a second World Cup star on England’s jersey now in tatters, focus turns to the home Euros of 2028.

Can Tuchel’s England end their long barren run without a trophy on home soil? Daily Mail Sport examines the big questions facing the national game.

ARE WE GOOD ENOUGH?

No, frankly, we are not. Not at the moment anyway. Perhaps the biggest disappointment of England’s time at this World Cup is that the national team still doesn’t have an identifiable style of play good enough to hurt the really good opponents.

After Gareth Southgate’s attempts to build a team in the image of some of our rivals on the continent, Tuchel said he wanted to construct one in the style of a Premier League side but when it came to the big tests, that wasn’t apparent.

Had England held on against Argentina and faced Spain in the final, it could have been embarrassing. We have good players who will get better. Jude Bellingham, Elliot Anderson, Declan Rice, Djed Spence and Anthony Gordon should all improve between now and the next summer tournament. But in terms of our ability to dictate games when it matters and against the best sides, England have stagnated and it’s a worry.

Watching a rerun of the last half hour from Atlanta, Argentina trampled all over us and could have scored four. England had twelve percent possession between scoring their goal and the end of the game. That’s not what a good team does.

Thomas Tuchel has still not given this England team an identifiable style good enough to hurt good teams

Argentina trampled all over England to produce the comeback victory in Atlanta

DECISIONS, DECISIONS...

History and culture don’t win football matches, players and coaches do. To win a tournament takes the right squad and a coach making the right decisions.

England’s World Cup squad was big on vibes and culture but, when it came down to it, low on technical and tactical smarts. This was an England squad that had Dan Burn, Jordon Henderson, Jarell Quansah and Trevoh Chalobah in it but no Cole Palmer, Phil Foden or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

Whoever you blame, there is something fundamentally wrong about that. When England needed it, we didn’t have the player to take control of a football game and dictate its direction and its rhythm.

Whatever happens between now and Euro 2028, we have to find a way to make our best players – our most technically gifted footballers – fundamental to how we play and what we do. Palmer would be in the Spain team so why isn’t he in ours?

CAN HARRY GO AGAIN?

So here we are. Back to the same old subject. Captain Kane had a fabulous tournament for England. Perhaps one of only three players – along with Bellingham and Anderson – to emerge from this World Cup with a mark of more than 6/10. But still England rely on him far too much.

Against Argentina, Kane laboured in the part of the game that really mattered. England needed someone up front to stretch the game. Every time we cleared the ball it came back again. But Tuchel kept Ollie Watkins and Marcus Rashford on the bench until it was too late.

The head coach doesn’t trust his Kane understudies and never has. Watkins played six minutes all tournament while Ivan Toney didn’t get a sniff until he was thrown on at the death against Argentina.

England have two years to find an answer to the problem. Kane will be almost 35 by then so the clock is ticking.

England still rely on Harry Kane far too much and Tuchel has two years to find the answer

WHERE IS THE HOPE?

English football is not short of emerging talent and, as we say, already has players in this World Cup squad with time to improve. Tuchel will hope for some real Arsenal game time for 16-year-old Max Dowman over the next season or so, for example.

Bellingham was only 17 when Gareth Southgate included him in his squad for the Euros of 2020 – delayed a year because of Covid – and he got limited minutes. But it was a vital part of Bellingham’s international education and that should be the path for Dowman now.

Elsewhere, Everton’s Tyler Dibling remains a huge prospect, despite a disappointing first season on Merseyside, while Rio Ngumoha of Liverpool should progress quickly now that Mo Salah is not standing in his way.

There is a worry at centre half. We need a ball carrier in that position. If anyone spots the next John Stones please shout.

ARE WE OVERREACTING?

No, we are not. Other European nations get it right so why can’t we? England came to America to win the World Cup and in terms of their football fell well short.

The statement from the FA that dropped after the whistle on Wednesday lamented the fact that it's ‘heartbreaking to be so close’ but the truth is that the way England played was well short of the required standard.

England fell well short of their ultimate goal of winning their second-ever World Cup

English football continues to face challenges with the schedule and the stakeholders must look again at a winter break. Two of Tuchel’s most important players – title winners Rice and Bukayo Saka – arrived at this tournament broken by the domestic season with Arsenal. Frankly, they played like it.

English football keeps telling itself that it has turned a corner in terms of styles of play, technical aptitude and player welfare. But the problem is that if you keep turning corners you end up back in the same place.

Sports.title: Inside Arsenal's 'patient' transfer window strategy: Why Andrea Berta is unfazed by lack of business, how 'machine' is working round the clock to secure bargains and the defender who could replace sidelined William Saliba
Sports.content:
Inside Arsenal's 'patient' transfer window strategy: Why Andrea Berta is unfazed by lack of business, how 'machine' is working round the clock to secure bargains and the defender who could replace sidelined William Saliba

Unlock more from Isaan Khan inside the Arsenal camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

‘Patience’ is the buzzword circulating around Arsenal’s London Colney base.

That might not appease large sections of the Premier League champions’ fanbase, with many supporters panicking at their lack of business so far.

But Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta are taking a measured approach, shaped by the unique challenges of a World Cup year and the need to carefully manage a squad already pushed to its physical limits.

The fan expectation stems from a more restrained strategy than last summer, when Berta had made six of his eight signings in July.

Those additions were Kepa Arrizabalaga, Martin Zubimendi, Christian Norgaard, Noni Madueke, Cristhian Mosquera and Viktor Gyokeres. They not only brought with them a great deal of excitement, but those moves left other clubs to sweat on deals, with Arsenal having done the bulk of their business way ahead of the deadline.

At present, the Gunners have only made one outfield signing heading towards the fourth week of July – and that was making Piero Hincapie’s loan deal permanent.

Arsenal made a raft of signings last July, including Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres (pictured), but have made a slower start to this summer's window

Sporting director Andrea Berta with new back-up goalkeeper Illan Meslier - the only fresh face in their 2026-27 squad as it stands

Goalkeeper Illan Meslier was signed on a free transfer from Leeds last week. He is expected to be third-choice between the sticks, behind David Raya and Kepa, but could be bumped up to second if the latter departs.

The World Cup has made negotiating deals tricky, with players focused on representing their country. With the tournament concluding on Sunday, there is an expectation that business at Arsenal will start to be ramped up from next week.

Berta has put in the groundwork. Sources say he’s a ‘machine’ who gets to the training ground early in the morning and doesn’t leave until late.

The Italian’s strategy will not be shaken by the lack of signatures so far. He negotiates multiple deals for a single position before pulling the trigger and deciding which player to move for.

It goes back to his days as a banker, a real-world business outlook transported into football. Each agent or club is left on edge wondering if Arsenal really want their player, reducing the likelihood of them strongarming the Gunners into paying way over the odds.

The approach is smart but not flawless. The dithering can cause a player to have his head turned elsewhere, to a different club who show more concrete interest — and more money. Jeremy Monga is a pertinent example, the 17-year-old set to join Arsenal before Manchester City swooped in with a better financial package.

Arsenal, though, have a different sway compared to many clubs. They are the reigning champions, which is a highly attractive proposition for suitors.

It’s understood that Berta refuses to be drawn into a deal which is not good monetary value for the club. The numbers matter to him, a different approach to some sporting directors who are more gung-ho financially.

Berta puts in the groundwork. Sources say he’s a ‘machine’ who gets to the training ground early in the morning and doesn’t leave until late

Left wing is a key area in which Arsenal need to strengthen now Leandro Trossard has joined Besiktas

Left wing is the key focus now Leandro Trossard has joined Besiktas, with the club closing in on Club Bruges winger Christos Tzolis. Berta’s assistant Maurizio Micheli watched the 24-year-old play for Greece against Sweden last month.

Even when the Gunners get their deal for Tzolis over the line, there is still capacity to bring in another forward, with firm interest remaining in Aston Villa’s Morgan Rogers.

The squad needs bolstering. There is an awareness at the club that the opening weeks of the league season present a need for immediate rotation, with many of their frontline players at breaking point.

Declan Rice was the Arsenal outfield player who accumulated the most minutes during the 2025-26 campaign, with 3,094 in the Premier League alone. He has battled through England’s World Cup with neural pain in his hamstring, which began around Christmas.

Bukayo Saka started 25 of Arsenal’s 38 league matches last season despite enduring injuries to his hamstring, hip and achilles. The achilles issue has plagued the winger since March, Thomas Tuchel revealing that Saka had carried on playing for Arsenal while not fully fit in the later months of the league campaign.

He added that the winger would be treated with care in his camp, a genuine concern given that the 24-year-old has played an awful lot of football in the past year. Saka made just two starts in England’s seven World Cup matches, and was an unused substitute in the 2-1 semi-final defeat by Argentina.

William Saliba has been dealing with a back issue which saw the 25-year-old manage just 30 minutes of France’s 2-0 semi-final loss to Spain on Tuesday. He trudged off the pitch, mouthing: ‘My back is gone’.

William Saliba will be out for months after trudging off in France's World Cup semi-final loss to Spain with a back issue

Arsenal will need to manage their squad carefully this season, with both Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice looking exhausted in the US

It’s understood that Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa is on Arsenal’s radar. He would have the potential to compete with Mosquera as the starting centre back in place of Saliba, who is set to miss at least the first few months of the season. However, the two clubs are some way apart in their valuations of the centre back.

Arsenal’s pre-season officially starts on Monday at London Colney, though players not at the World Cup are currently in a Marbella camp with Arteta and his staff.

For Arsenal, the message remains clear: patience will win out over panic. The next few weeks will determine whether Berta’s calculated approach delivers the final pieces Arteta needs to defend their title.

Sports.title: Oliver Glasner's to-do list: The gap in Nottingham Forest squad he's close to filling, keeping Evangelos Marinakis happy - and the line at his unveiling that set him apart from his predecessors
Sports.content:
Oliver Glasner has been at Nottingham Forest for only three days but already his in-tray is filling up.

The Austrian has five weeks to reconfigure his team’s tactics, establish who he can rely on and – crucially – identify his principal centre forward for the campaign ahead.

Glasner cut a relaxed figure when he was introduced to the media at the City Ground on Thursday, cracking jokes about his first date with his wife, but he knows the honeymoon period will be brief.

Daily Mail Sport looks at the main challenges facing Glasner as he tries to ensure his team hit the ground running when they face Leeds on August 22.

Oliver Glasner cut a relaxed figure at the City Ground on Thursday, cracking jokes about his first date with his wife, but he knows the honeymoon period will be brief

The Austrian has had huge success with a 3-4-2-1 system and it would be a surprise if he deviated from it significantly at Nottingham Forest

The missing pieces

At Crystal Palace, Glasner had huge success with a 3-4-2-1 system that proved hugely effective on the counter-attack – though breaking down defensive teams was often a problem.

He insists he has yet to decide between a back three and a back four and was at pains to say he does not want to create ‘Palace Two’ at Forest. Yet given the success he had in south London, it would be a surprise to see Forest line up radically differently.

Glasner intends to play with two No 10s behind a lone front man. Expect one of these to be Morgan Gibbs-White – assuming the Forest captain stays – with the other spot up for grabs. Forest are pursuing Tottenham midfielder Lucas Bergvall strongly.

Glasner namechecked Omari Hutchinson and James McAtee in his opening remarks, referencing Hutchinson’s ability to cut inside and shoot on his left foot. As long as Hutchinson has a decent pre-season, we can expect him to figure strongly in the early weeks of the new campaign.

Yet where Hutchinson improved as the season progressed, McAtee struggled throughout and made only 13 starts – two in the league. Just because McAtee is praised by the manager on July 16, that does not guarantee he will be at Forest when the summer window closes.

Perhaps, though, Glasner could be the coach to bring the best from McAtee, who is talented but suffers in the ultra-athletic modern game. If he has mentioned McAtee, it is because Glasner believes he can improve him.

Morgan Gibbs-White will almost certainly be one of Glasner's No10s behind the striker

Elliot Anderson was sold to Manchester City for £116million and Glasner accepts he cannot replace him with one player only. Xaver Schlager is set to join on a free transfer after leaving RB Leipzig and may line up alongside Ibrahim Sangare in the middle of the park, with the Ivory Coast star set to sign a new deal.

While there are plenty of defensive options, right back and No9 are key.

There is an acceptance at Forest that due to his injury record, Ola Aina needs a proven alternative, while Chris Wood turns 35 in December. Forest will be prepared to invest significantly in both areas, and Glasner sidestepped questions about whether he would target Palace players. Daniel Munoz and Jean-Philippe Mateta would certainly help this squad, though.

Glasner’s bold approach

Since Steve Cooper transformed Forest in 2021, leading them from the bottom of the Championship to promotion later that season, all managers have followed him in leaning heavily into Forest’s history.

The club won consecutive European Cups in 1979 and 1980 under Brian Clough, and memories of those days are on display across the City Ground. It would have been easy for Glasner to celebrate that as his predecessors did. He chose not to.

‘It’s a club with huge history but if we all lived as we did 46 years ago, we would fail,’ he said. ‘It’s good to have a great history but great history doesn’t tell anything about the future.

‘We want to make a step forward. Now is our fifth year in the Premier League and it doesn’t make sense talking about the European Cup trophies. Let’s get consistency into Forest in every way.’

It was a bold step and proves Glasner is not here to toe the line. Having won four major trophies (three with Palace and one with Frankfurt) Glasner has huge confidence in his own ability and is not afraid to show it.

Nor will he be afraid to put pressure on the ownership, or to make his feelings known if he is not given what he believes he needs. Indeed, there were plenty of clashes like these during his two-and-a-half years at Palace.

Unlike his predecessors, Glasner did not pay lip service to Forest's European Cup wins under Brian Clough

‘It’s important we stick to what we tell each other as it builds trust and we all want to feel that,’ said Glasner. ‘It’s like friendships or relationships. If someone tells you something and doesn't stick to their word, you don’t trust them anymore.’

Evangelos Marinakis does not mind the odd forthright back-and-forth with a manager and with Glasner, he will surely have his fair share.

Aiming high

Marinakis is the most ambitious owner in the Premier League, bar none. He believes Forest can break into the wealthy elite and become Champions League regulars. As Glasner acknowledged: ‘He is one of the few people I’ve met who are more ambitious than I am and that’s quite difficult. We will challenge each other with our ambition.’

It is very easy in July to talk about stability and consistency. It is a little more difficult if a club invests heavily and are 14th in the table at Christmas. Glasner pointed out that Forest’s league finishes had not always reflected their transfer spending and it is now for him to put that right.

In theory, Glasner’s brief will be to turn Forest into a club who compete regularly in the top half of the table and eventually push for Europe. In practice, he will be expected to hit the ground running.

Talented centre back Murillo will stay at the City Ground unless Forest receive an offer wildly above his market value

Unless they receive offers wildly above their market values, Forest have no plans to sell Gibbs-White, Neco Williams or Murillo. In return, Marinakis will expect no struggles in the bottom half of the table.

Glasner will not worry about these tasks. He has already chosen a difficult route by opting for Forest, who are disliked intensely by Palace these days after the Eagles were demoted to the Conference League a year ago due to UEFA rules, allowing Forest to step into the Europa League. He does not worry, he insists, about whether he’ll become Forest’s fifth managerial casualty in a relatively short time, after Nuno Espirito Santo, Ange Postecoglou, Sean Dyche and Vitor Pereira.

One word of advice, though, Oliver: get a couple of wins on the board early.

Sports.title: The FA's gamble on Thomas Tuchel has failed. He was outcoached and turned to neanderthal football. Now I fear what comes next, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel was supposed to be the man who would turn water into wine. That was what the Football Association told us. That was the rationale for turning its back on the work that Gareth Southgate had done with the England team and paying big money for a quick-fix super-coach who would win the World Cup.

When Southgate left after the 2024 European Championship, the FA chose not to build on what he achieved. They did not have the courage to do what the Spanish Football Federation did when they promoted Luis de la Fuente, a successful coach of its youth teams, to the senior job when Luis Enrique left after the 2022 World Cup.

Lee Carsley had won the European Under-21 Championship with England – and won it again last year – but was deemed not good enough by the FA, who abandoned their principles of a coaching pathway for English talent by appointing a foreign manager.

The rationale for deviating from a path that had brought significant steps forward in the evolution of the England team – England reached the final of the European Championship in 2021 and 2024 and the semi-finals of the World Cup in 2018 – was that England needed a coach of Tuchel’s proven talent at club level to take them over the final step.

It was a high-stakes gamble and on Wednesday night, that gamble failed. When England lost to Argentina in the Atlanta Stadium, blowing a 1-0 lead, the tactical sophistication that Tuchel had promised was replaced with neanderthal football.

England invited wave after wave of Argentina attacks. They gave Lionel Messi, the greatest player the world has ever seen, time and space. They seemed surprised when Messi laid on two goals in seven minutes in the dying stages of the game.

Thomas Tuchel was supposed to be the man who would turn water into wine. But he couldn't live up to that reputation

Not only did England lose to Argentina, but they lost playing neanderthal football

‘I found it absolutely unfathomable,’ former England striker Gary Lineker said after the match, ‘that, if your tactic is to sit everyone deep, you do that against the greatest player ever to play football.’

From Anthony Gordon’s goal in the 55th minute until the Lautaro Martinez winner in the 92nd minute, England had just 12 per cent possession. Twelve per cent. Let that sink in. It felt as if England were playing with 10 men. Or nine men. And for all his attempts at excuses about sloppy technique and different football cultures, that was on Tuchel. That was squarely on Tuchel.

What really hurts is this: the single most obvious truth from Wednesday night is that Tuchel was outcoached by Lionel Scaloni. Comprehensively outcoached. Scaloni’s substitutions were positive and proactive for a start. Tuchel’s were overwhelmingly negative and cautious. They handed the momentum to an Argentina team that was there for the taking.

Scaloni, another coach, like De la Fuente, promoted from his country’s youth system, spoke after the game about the period following England’s goal, when England should have pressed home their advantage but instead, led by Tuchel’s negative substitutions, played as if they were scared of victory.

He and his players sensed Tuchel’s hesitation. They sensed his uncertainty. They sensed his lack of faith in his players’ technical ability. ‘There was blood in the water,’ Scaloni said, ‘and we went for it.’ Blood in the water? England had just gone 1-0 up and there was blood in the water. What an indictment of Tuchel’s coaching that is.

And if there is seething anger among England fans at falling one hurdle short of a first World Cup final for 60 years, it is because they have seen this movie before. We have all seen this movie before. England always find a way to lose the big games at major tournaments. We were told it would be different this time because of Tuchel. But it wasn’t different. It was almost exactly the same. If anything, it was worse.

Tuchel's uncertainty and lack of faith in his players invited Argentina to go for the jugular

Once again, England took the lead in a big game, and once again they blew it. That's on Tuchel

That is one of the reasons why there is so much disillusion with the manner of England’s capitulation. It fits a pattern: England have often led in the match in which they are eventually knocked out. It was the case in 1996 against Germany, 1998 against Argentina, 2002 against Brazil, 2004 against Portugal, 2016 against Iceland, 2018 against Croatia and 2021 against Italy. It is a cruel way to lose. Now, it has happened again.

Tuchel did his best to avoid the blame in Atlanta. He blamed almost everything else instead. Without naming individuals, he had criticised his players for ‘sloppy’ technical mistakes after the fortunate win over Norway in the quarter-finals and he hinted at similar issues after the semi-final defeat.

But England’s World Cup failure was on him. Not the players. If anything, the players bailed him out at this tournament. Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane bailed him out. It doesn’t wash for Tuchel to start criticising his players’ technical abilities. He knew their abilities when he signed on to win the World Cup.

And, by the way, the England player with the best technique, a player who can change games with his awareness and his ability, is Cole Palmer. And Tuchel didn’t even include Palmer in his squad.

Tuchel did not turn water into wine. He turned it into vinegar. He led England to the semi-finals of the World Cup but his part in the capitulation to Argentina has soured everything. England were in sight of their first World Cup final for 60 years but instead of helping them to the line, Tuchel brought them to their knees.

The FA will not sack Tuchel because they have just given him a two-year extension to his contract but the manner of England’s exit from the World Cup and the disillusion it has spread means that they are stuck with a lame-duck manager to lead them into a home Euros in 2028.

Tuchel's substitution of Anthony Gordon for Ezri Konsa will go down in infamy

Tuchel’s history suggests that when things start to go south for him in a job, they go south very quickly. The worry for the FA, and for England fans, is that Wednesday’s semi-final defeat will be the prelude to a period when the coach’s relationship with them and his players goes downhill fast.

Whatever happens, he will be remembered as the coach who took off Anthony Gordon and replaced him with Ezri Konsa in the 72nd minute.

As substitutions go, it will stand there in infamy alongside Sir Alf Ramsey’s decision to take off Bobby Charlton when England led West Germany in the quarter-finals of the 1970 World Cup.

Whether he makes it through to the Euros or whether he departs then, there will be no escaping his legacy. When England had their best chance of reaching the World Cup final for 60 years, Tuchel blew it.

Sports.title: Crying Jude Bellingham is consoled by his parents and WAG Ashlyn Castro after England's World Cup semi-final heartbreak
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham fought back tears as he was comforted by family and friends after England's World Cup campaign came to an end with a defeat to Argentina in Atlanta last night.

The Real Madrid midfielder, arguably the Three Lions' standout player of the tournament, was unable to reproduce the heroics that led his team to victory over Norway as they fell to a 2-1 defeat against the defending world champions.

Anthony Gordon had given England the lead before Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez struck late on to book Argentina's place in Sunday's showpiece at the New York-New Jersey Stadium.

Long after the final whistle, and following a feisty confrontation with Argentina substitute Valentin Barco, Bellingham turned to his family for support.

Footage showed the Real Madrid star embracing his father, Mark Bellingham, and mother, Denise Bellingham, while wiping away tears. His close friend and England team-mate Morgan Rogers was also seen hugging his parents.

The 23-year-old was also spotted sitting alongside his girlfriend, Ashlyn Castro, 28, appearing visibly downcast by the afternoon's events.

Footage showed the Real Madrid star embracing his father, Mark Bellingham, while wiping away tears

The Real Madrid star was spotted sitting alongside his girlfriend, Ashlyn Castro, 28, appearing visibly downcast by the afternoon's events

The pair were joined by Bellingham's father, Mark, and his mother, Denise, in the stands after the final whistle

It was a change in mood from what had preceded it, with Bellingham having become embroiled in a heated altercation with Barco in the moments after the final whistle.

Bellingham slapped the young Strasbourg player's head from behind, sparking a brief melee involving players from both sides.

It remains unclear what triggered the reaction from the Real Madrid midfielder, though footage has circulated showing Barco running onto the pitch after Fernandez's 85th-minute equaliser and celebrating in front of the England players rather than joining his team-mates by the corner flag.

Former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson, commentating for BBC Radio 5 Live, described Barco's actions as 'probably the worst example of sportsmanship we've seen at this World Cup'.

Barco, 21, plays for French side Strasbourg and previously spent time at Brighton. He is reportedly set to join Chelsea ahead of the upcoming Premier League season.

The Argentine has featured just once at the tournament, coming off the bench in the second half of his side's 3-1 group-stage victory over Jordan.

The match itself was incredibly attritional, with 19 fouls committed in the first half, as American referee Ismail Elfath struggled to keep a lid on things.

In the very first minute, Alexis Mac Allister set the tone for what was about to unfold, flooring Elliot Anderson just 19 seconds after the first whistle.

A few minutes later, Bellingham appeared to confront Messi for another foul on Anderson.

'We were really just discussing a foul, actually,' Bellingham is reported to have said after the match.

'It wasn't anything bad. I'm sure everyone will do their thing and make it a big deal, but it was nothing.'

Join the discussion What do you think England needs to do differently before the next major tournament?

Bellingham became embroiled in a heated altercation with Argentina substitute Valentin Barco in the moments after the final whistle

'I wish I could say more. I wish I could give one more win or two more wins. But at the moment I'm kind of - my head's a bit fuzzy with disappointment,' he said in his post-match interview

As for his post-match assessment, Bellingham said: 'I think we can take a lot from the experience, but it's so gutting.

'I wanted to be a part of an England squad that had finally done it, finally got it over the line. And to be here telling the fans unfortunately the same things that they've probably heard for years and years, it's really gutting.

'I wish I could say more. I wish I could give one more win or two more wins. But at the moment I'm kind of - my head's a bit fuzzy with disappointment.'

During the post-match celebrations, Argentina's stars held aloft a banner that read: 'The Malvinas (Falklands) are ours.'

That has led to calls for the players involved to face disciplinary action from FIFA.

Despite FIFA's ban on political flags, Tottenham captain Romero, Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez and ex-Spurs midfielder Giovani Lo Celso celebrated with the controversial sign after the final whistle.

Captain and star player Messi was also seen dancing alongside the banner.

FIFA has yet to comment, but the governing body is under huge pressure to punish Argentina for flouting its rules. Manchester United and Spurs are being urged to punish Martinez and Romero.

Twelve years ago, the team carried the same banner at an international friendly and was fined just £20,000.

But there are growing calls for the players who carried the banner at a match of such magnitude - watched by an estimated 950million people worldwide - to face tougher sanctions.

Sports.title: Now England fans claim Argentina's winning goal shouldn't have stood! Lionel Messi appears to foul Three Lions star in build up to decisive strike in World Cup semi-final defeat
Sports.content:
Now England fans claim Argentina's winning goal shouldn't have stood! Lionel Messi appears to foul Three Lions star in build up to decisive strike in World Cup semi-final defeat

CHAT: Should Thomas Tuchel be sacked? Join our debate now

How much is David Beckham set to pocket from his World Cup brand deals? Take on our quiz in our newsletter HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Furious England fans have claimed Argentina's winning goal should not have stood due to an apparent foul by Lionel Messi in the build-up.

The Three Lions threw away a 1-0 lead with five minutes of normal time remaining to lose 2-1 in the World Cup semi-final.

After Anthony Gordon put Thomas Tuchel's men in front, England were pegged back by an Enzo Fernandez strike on 85 minutes before Lautaro Martinez sealed their fate in second-half stoppage time.

However, Martinez's goal has left many England supporters fuming - with some claiming that Argentina talisman Messi had fouled defender Djed Spence just moments before.

After Alexis Mac Allister hit the post for the second time, the ball cannoned back out on England's left-hand side, leading to a foot race between Spence and Messi in the penalty area. Spence beat Messi to the ball but appeared to be caught by Messi in the process.

Immediately the full back spun around in some discomfort but referee Ismael Elfath waved play on. And just seconds later England were punished as Messi crossed to an unmarked Martinez to score.

Argentina are ahead! 😱



A relentless spell of pressure sees Alexis Mac Allister hit the post before ANOTHER Lionel Messi assist sets up Lautaro Martinez to make it 2-1. pic.twitter.com/kVoNouFgKZ — BBC Sport (@BBCSport) July 15, 2026

Many England fans feel Lionel Messi (right) fouled Djed Spence prior to Argentina's winner

The pair both sprinted for a 50/50 duel which Spence won just ahead of Messi

However, Spence was soon turning around in discomfort in the aftermath as play continued

And taking to social media, England fans have questioned why VAR didn't get involved to overturn the decision.

'Messi's stamp on Spence before Lautaro's goal, why does VAR only work when the goal is against Argentina?' wrote one user on X, before doubling down with: 'No foul X, no VAR check X, Goal allowed [tick].'

'How was that not called as a foul,' remarked another; while another user put: 'Spence should have gone down and rolled around here, worked for them all game.'

In another post, a user wrote: 'Serious question… why was Messi stepping on Djed Spence completely ignored seconds before Argentina's second goal?

'Spence was visibly limping afterwards and could barely defend the next phase, yet VAR never appeared to review the incident. How can a potential foul directly affecting the goal be brushed aside that easily?'

Another questioned: 'Surely Messi fouled Spence here. How did this not get called back [?]'

Despite their protestations, many took to social media to defend Messi and insist that there was no contact made between the pair.

Irrespective of whether or not there was contact, England fans were largely in unison in directing their anger towards head coach Thomas Tuchel for his defensive second-half substitutions when they were winning.

Surely Messi fouled Spence here. How did this not get called back pic.twitter.com/2LWzXjSjUS — Jack (@jruttan0) July 15, 2026

They had plenty of duels during the World Cup semi-final showdown, which Argentina won 2-1

Lautaro Martinez (centre) rises high to head home Argentina's winner to send them through

However, the German remained defiant post-match - defending his tactics and insisting he had 'no regrets'.

'We were so close but we got too passive after we scored and conceded a lot of chances and could not turn the ball possession around. We conceded so many crosses and chances and shots,' Tuchel said after the match.

'We were close but we could not keep the level up after we scored.'

'Of course we wanted to go for the second goal, but I did not feel an offensive substitution would help. We stayed in our 4-4-2 but became passive and we couldn't win any balls and couldn't keep the ball, so I don't think it was a structural problem.'

'No regrets, the team gave everything and we were very very close. We deserved to be up one nil, we played one of our better matches, maybe the best match, at the moment, no regrets.'

Sports.title: Smug Lionel Messi gloats 'England didn't want it anymore' after sending Three Lions home from the World Cup
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi twisted the knife at full-time as he claimed that England 'didn't want' to win a place in the World Cup final after their heartbreaking defeat to Argentina in Atlanta.

The diminutive playmaker captained his side to a 2-1 win after Enzo Fernandez sparked a late comeback with his 85th-minute equaliser.

But it was Lautaro Martinez who extinguished any faint hope of pinching something in extra-time with his goal in the 92nd minute, which booked Argentina their second-consecutive chance to claim the trophy in New York.

After the final whistle, Messi reserved praise for the Argentina fans inside the stadium, but added that he believed the last-gasp victory had stemmed from their opponents' dwindling fight.

'We felt a lot of emotion, and when we were drawing, we needed the support of the fans, because we saw that we could win it in 90 minutes,' he said.

'Because we already had the goal, because we entered through the inside, the outside, because we created opportunities with crosses, through line passes, through the inside.

Lionel Messi claimed that Argentina had been the ones who wanted to win a place in the World Cup final - not England

The national team captain celebrated wildly with his side in front of the fans holding a banner supporting Argentina's claim to the Falkland Islands

'And we felt they didn't want it anymore and we just kept coming, that's why after the 1-1, the crowd helped us again once more, and as I said, we are happy because it was a close match.

'We always want to win, and also because it takes us to play another World Cup final.'

Thomas Tuchel has come under heavy criticism for his tactics following Anthony Gordon's opening goal in the 55th minute, with the manager bringing on a raft of defensive substitutes to see out the game.

Gordon, Reece James and Declan Rice were exchanged for Ezri Konsa, Nico O'Reilly, and Dan Burn, reshaping England's midfield and leaving them with little room to foment attacking threat in case of Argentina equalising.

When Argentina duly did, Tuchel waited until the dying minutes of injury time to throw on Ivan Toney and Marcus Rashford in place of defensive options John Stones and Djed Spence - but it was too little, too late.

World Cup-winning goalkeeper with Spain Iker Casillas described the decision as 'cowardly' from England, while Chris Sutton claimed that Tuchel had suffered a 'coaching catastrophe'.

On his Overlap podcast the following morning, Gary Neville suggested that captain Harry Kane should have been the one subbed off, with players who could become the sharp point of a potential counter-attack like Rashford on in his place.

Neville's viewpoint about the defensive changes was echoed by former England team-mate Ian Wright, who said: 'For me, he's made substitutions that are not attacking, they're defending.

'For a manager that's been as brave as he's been with the selections from the start, with the players that he's brought in, were the selections and the substitutions he made up to this point positive in that game?'

Speaking post-match, Tuchel insisted he had 'no regrets' with his second-half tactics and said England played their 'best game' of the tournament on Wednesday.

Despite not getting on the scoresheet on Wednesday evening, Messi still found himself in the headlines after the Inter Miami star became embroiled in a testy exchange of words with Jude Bellingham.

Join the discussion Do you agree with Messi’s assessment of England’s performance?

Messi was earlier in the match involved in a testy discussion with Jude Bellingham

It came after players from both teams were involved in an altercation after a foul, with the duo seemingly in a charged conversation for several moments.

Messi was then captured staring at Bellingham's retreating back after the England star walked away from him, before making a sarcastic gesture which seemed to imply he disagreed with the Real Madrid man.

The former Barcelona star was also captured dancing alongside a banner unfurled by members of the Argentina squad which laid claim to the Falkland Islands.

FIFA has yet to comment, but the governing body is under huge pressure to punish Argentina for flouting its rules with an incendiary banner backing the country's claim to the Falkland Islands.

Manchester United and Tottenham are being urged to punish players who participated in the stunt, including Spurs' captain Cristian Romero, and Lisandro Martinez.

Twelve years ago, the team carried the same banner at an international friendly and was fined just £20,000.

But there are growing calls for the players who carried the banner at a match of such magnitude - watched by an estimated 950 million people worldwide - to face tougher sanctions.

Sports.title: Former England Lioness celebrates Argentina star boyfriend's World Cup win over Thomas Tuchel's side after stirring controversy for supporting reigning champions
Sports.content:
Former England Lioness Kelci-Rose Bowers celebrated her partner Marcos Senesi's success with Argentina after the team beat England to reach the World Cup semi-final.

The 22-year-old had previously shared that she would have divided loyalties heading into the clash, and admitting that she knew that her choice would be 'controversial'.

After the heartbreaking defeat that saw Thomas Tuchel and Co knocked out thanks to Lautaro Martinez's late winner, Bowers - who plays for Bournemouth and previously featured in England's youth ranks - shared that she was 'proud of her country :((' while simultaneously 'proud of (Senesi)' always as she opened up on the difficulties of supporting both sides.

'Well that just happened…,' she shared in a grid post to Instagram. 'Of course a crazy experience with a lot of mixed emotions, one I won’t forget (England flag emoji, Argentina flag emoji, prayer hands emoji)

'I am proud of how far England have come and of course my partner for reaching the WC FINAL (heart-eyes emojis)

'See you in NYC (arrow emoji)'.

Kelci-Rose Bowers - whose partner is Argentina star Marcos Senesi - shared a message full of 'mixed emotions' after his team knocked out England

The WAG and Bournemouth women's team star played for England's Lionesses at youth level

Bowers shared snaps from the stadium, including a look at the England fans in the stands and players from the pitch - but did so while sitting in the thick of Argentina's friends and family support.

She did however draw the line at donning the iconic blue and white stripes of the Albiceleste, instead opting for a pinstriped jacket by team sponsor adidas.

Before the match had kicked off, Bowers had taken to TikTok to explain why she would above all else be supporting Senesi on the eve of one of her country's most significant international fixtures.

'Crazy situation, didn't think this was actually going to happen,' she said. 'It's crazy that England are playing Argentina in the semi-final, that's not happened in forever.

'This situation is very unusual for me, of course, being English and England making it to the semi-final is a crazy accomplishment and I'm super proud of my country.

'Of course my partner is playing for Argentina so for anyone in any relationship, depending on what your partner does, you're going to support them. For me, being able to come to the World Cup and travel around has been amazing.

'Embracing the culture of Argentina and wearing the Argentina shirt has been something that I've been doing - and I don't think there's anything wrong with it.

'Now England are playing Argentina there is some controversy about what I'm going to do. Look, I'm going to go to the game, enjoy the game, respect both teams and cheer on my partner. I'm just there to enjoy it guys.'

From the Argentina team's friends and family section, Bowers shared pictures of the stadium

But Bowers did not sport the blue and white striped jersey of the Albiceleste at this fixture, as she has earlier in the tournament (pictured)

The 22-year-old has been following Argentina since Senesi's late call-up to the team in June

Bowers had previously captured Senesi's euphoric reaction to his late call-up while the couple were enjoying their summer holiday.

The newly minted Tottenham star was called upon by head coach Lionel Scaloni to travel Stateside following an injury to Leonardo Balerdi during their training camp.

Senesi and Bowers had been enjoying holidays in Miami and then Ibiza before he got the call.

The duo first met at the south coast club in 2024, with Bowers turning out for the women's side and Senesi for the men's.

The latter has since booked a move to north London side Spurs, inking a deal with the club last month as a free transfer.

When all is said and done, the onus lies with Thomas Tuchel and his men for not doing enough to get the job done in Atlanta. After all, they would have been within their rights to fight fire with fire and deploy the same dark arts as their opponents.

That doesn't make it any easier to swallow a particularly bitter pill, however. And it becomes that much more difficult to accept when breaking down the sheer quantity of underhanded offences Argentina were guilty of en route to a 2-1 comeback win.
